## 2. Configuring the simulator

There are four configuration surfaces. Most users only touch the env
vars in 2.1.

### 2.1 Environment variables (the only ones you usually set)

`setup.sh` exports these for you. Override only if your artifacts live
somewhere non-default.

| Variable        | Default                                          | Used by                  |
|-----------------|--------------------------------------------------|--------------------------|
| `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` | From `config.env` (sec 1.3); toolchain root  | Makefile, NM derivation  |
| `VSIM_QEMU`     | `$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64` (external)    | every harness            |
| `VSIM_PLUGIN`   | `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so`               | every harness            |
| `VSIM_BIN`      | first `$VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_*`                     | every harness            |
| `VSIM_ELF`      | `tests/fixtures/$FIXTURE.elf`           | harness scripts          |
| `NM`            | `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm`   | PC-mode symbol resolve   |
| `TIMEOUT`       | 60 s (120 for long runs)                         | per-leg `timeout` cap    |
| `FIXTURE`       | `rt_shared_mem`                                  | which `.elf` to load     |
| `TRIGGER_MODE`  | `marker`                                            | `marker` or `pc`            |
| `JOBS`          | auto-cap on this 128-core host: set to 8         | parallel test runner     |
| `HSIM_MMAP_DIR` | tier list (`/dev/shm`, then `~/.cache/andesim`) | pin one backing dir for `--mem-size` (disables the fallback) |

Example: override the QEMU binary for one run:

```sh
VSIM_QEMU=/opt/qemu-9.0/qemu-system-riscv64 \
  ./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium
```

### 2.2 The vsim CPU configuration YAML

vsim is built in its own external checkout (the `hybrid_vsim` repo, pointed at by
`VSIM_BIN_DIR`); the commands in this section run THERE, not in andesim. Its
`config.yaml` selects which Andes core to verilate. The default is
`ax45mpv_premium`:

```yaml
cpus:
  ax45mpv_premium:
    cpu_series: 45
    rtl_package: ax45mpv_premium
    cpp_wrapper: ax45mpv_premium_cpu_cluster_subsystem
    config: data/configs/ax45mpv_premium.cfg
    config_dir: andes_ip/kv_core/top/hdl
    config_inc_filter: grep '^`define NDS_'
    extra_verilator_flags: --threads 8 --unroll-count 256
```

Switch CPU by pointing CMake at a different YAML (in your vsim checkout):

```sh
cd <your vsim checkout>   # e.g. /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DVSIM_CONFIG_FILE=my_other_cpu.yaml
cmake --build build -j
```

`-DVSIM_NO_VERILATOR=ON` skips Verilator (use a prebuilt model). The
hybrid doctest unit tests are always registered with CTest (run via
`ctest` or the `check` target).

### 2.3 QEMU plugin args

The plugin reads `arg=value` tokens after `-plugin <path>,`. They
select WHICH switching mode QEMU1 runs in:

| Plugin arg           | Effect                                                                 |
|----------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `outfile=PATH`       | REQUIRED. Drained `hybrid_state_v1` is written here.                   |
| `enter_pc=0xADDR`    | PC mode: drain when PC == ADDR. Bypasses the marker-insn matcher.         |
| `exit_marker=1`      | Oracle exit drain (verification): arm on the EXIT marker `slti x0,x0,0x5A1`, drain right after it retires. The run never hands off -- it produces the reference state `--verify` compares against. Exclusive with the other mode args. |
| `exit_pc=0xADDR`     | Oracle exit drain, pc form: arm when PC == ADDR instead of on the exit marker. |
| `drain_pc=0xADDR`    | Oracle modifier: after arming, drain at the first hit of ADDR (the verifier passes vsim's drained pc here, so both sides sample the same architectural point -- vsim's DMI halt lands a few insns past the trigger). |
| `ilm_size=BYTES`, `dlm_size=BYTES` | LM content transport: additionally drain that many bytes of ILM/DLM content (read through the hart-0 local-memory slave ports) into raw sidecar files `<outfile>.ilm` / `<outfile>.dlm`. Default 0 = skip (engine without that local memory); the driver passes the paired engine's sizes. |
| `ilm_base=0xADDR`, `dlm_base=0xADDR` | Override the LM slave-port bases (defaults `0xA0000000` / `0xA0200000`, AE350 hart 0). |
| `hvm_size=BYTES`     | HVM content transport: drain that many bytes of the High-Bandwidth Vector Memory into `<outfile>.hvm`, same contract as the LM sidecars. Default 0 = skip. |
| `hvm_base=0xADDR`    | Override the HVM subordinate-port base (default `0x90000000`, AE350). |

If no mode arg is given, the default is marker-insn match (marker mode): the
plugin matches `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` at retire.

Example invocation (marker mode, just the minimal arg):

```
-plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=/tmp/state.bin
```

### 2.4 vsim CLI flags

`sim_ax45mpv_premium <elf> [flags]`. The hybrid-relevant subset:

| Flag                          | Purpose                                                  |
|-------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| `--resume-from-qemu FILE`     | Read drained state, restore into hart, run from PC.     |
| `--handoff-out FILE`          | Drain back into FILE when the exit trigger fires.       |
| `--shared-mem-path FILE`      | mmap FILE as RAM (zero-copy share with QEMU).           |
| `--shared-mem-size BYTES`     | Size of the shared region. Match QEMU `-m`.             |
| `--shared-mem-base HEX`       | Guest physical address where file offset 0 lands.       |
| `--hybrid-exit-pc 0xADDR`     | PC mode exit: drain when this PC retires.               |
| `--drain-minimal`             | Exit drain reads back only mcycle/minstret; the driver sets it when `--verify` is off. |
| `--no-reset-baseline`         | Disable the liveness gate (below): restore every transported register. |
| `--jtag-port N`               | Open the JTAG bitbang port (ICEman or OpenOCD). The hart free-runs; the debugger halts it over the JTAG DTM on connect. The `./andesim run --mode cycle --gdb` path opens this port for ICEman (set `$ICEMAN`). |
| `--log-level N`               | 0=trace .. 5=critical .. 6=off (default 2=info)         |

`--shared-mem-base` must be the guest physical address of RAM: `0x0` on the
`andes_ae350` machine (its DRAM window is `0x0..0x7fffffff`; `0x80000000` is
the boot MROM, and vsim's built-in `0x80000000` default targets the upstream
`virt` machine). The driver always passes `0x0`; only standalone vsim
invocations need to override it.

**Liveness gate (reset baseline).** Every register moved through the Debug
Module costs hundreds of simulated cycles, and most transported state still
holds its reset value. So the resume skips any restore whose drained value
equals the engine's own reset value -- a no-op write. The very first hybrid
run of a given (engine build, ELF) pair drains that reset state once (a few
extra seconds) and caches it under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim/` (fallback
`~/.cache/andesim/`); later runs load the cache and typically cut the vsim
leg by ~4x (hello: 50k -> 12k simulated cycles). The cache self-invalidates
on engine rebuild or ELF change (mtime+size keyed); delete the directory to
force a fresh capture. `--verify` works unchanged with the gate active;
`--no-reset-baseline` restores the old transport-everything behavior.

Run `$VSIM_BIN --help` for the full list (waveform/save/restore are
license-gated and off by default).

### 2.5 Requesting memory (`--mem-size` + `HSIM_MMAP_DIR`)

By default every `./andesim` invocation that needs a shared mmap allocates
a 128 MiB sparse file under `/dev/shm` (tmpfs, RAM-backed). When your
workload's memory footprint exceeds `/dev/shm` capacity (typically
RAM/2 on Linux), two knobs let you redirect:

| Knob              | Where             | What it does |
|-------------------|-------------------|--------------|
| `--mem-size SPEC` | flag on `run` (`--mmap-size` is the old alias) | request guest program memory (`SPEC` = `128M`, `1.5G`, `2G`, or raw bytes). Cap `2G` minus one 4 KiB V-transport page (the AE350 DRAM window). |
| `HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/path` | env var | pin the backing directory (skips the tier list below). |

Per-model semantics of `--mem-size`:

| Model    | What it does |
|----------|--------------|
| `hybrid` | `--mem-size` is your **program** RAM (default `128M`). The driver maps one extra 4 KiB page on top for the V-register transport scratch (L26): the physical shared mmap = QEMU memory backend = vsim RAM window = `--mem-size + 4 KiB`, with the scratch parked in that top page, just above everything your program can address. You get your full `--mem-size`; the page is invisible. The driver rejects `> 2G - 4 KiB` **before** allocating, and rejects an ELF whose static image would extend into the reserved page (`raise --mem-size`). |
| `fast`   | forwards a plain QEMU `-m`. Without the flag the argv is untouched -- QEMU as-is, its own 128 MiB default, no mmap involved. No `2G` cap here (that ceiling is the hybrid shared-mmap window, not fast's); QEMU itself validates the size and rejects only oversized values (`Cannot model more than 16GB RAM` on the AE350 machine). |
| `cycle`  | validate-only: the cycle engine always models its full DRAM window, so there is nothing to size (the driver says so on stderr). |

Backing-directory selection (`./andesim`): a two-tier list, first fit
wins (fit = size + 256 MiB free):

1. `/dev/shm` -- tmpfs, RAM speed. Skipped when absent or too small.
2. `~/.cache/andesim` (honors `XDG_CACHE_HOME`) -- disk-backed; the
   size ceiling becomes disk free space. Hot pages still sit in the
   kernel page cache, so the cost vs tmpfs is background writeback only.

We never switch **silently**: the status line always names the chosen
dir, and a fallback adds the reason, e.g.
`[hsim mmap] 2.0 GiB at /home/u/.cache/andesim (free: 2.1 TiB) (fallback: /dev/shm too small (1.2 GiB free))`.
`HSIM_MMAP_DIR` pins a single dir with **no** fallback past it: rc=2
with a hint if it can't hold the request.

Examples:

```sh
# Small request; /dev/shm fits, so tier 1 is chosen.
./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 256M
#   [hsim mmap] 256.0 MiB at /dev/shm (free: 252.0 GiB)

# Near-max request on a small-RAM box: falls through to the disk tier,
# and the status line says so. (2047M is the hybrid ceiling -- exactly 2G is
# rejected because the extra V-scratch page would overflow the DRAM window.)
./andesim run my.elf --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 2047M
#   [hsim mmap] 2.0 GiB at /home/u/.cache/andesim (free: 2.1 TiB) (fallback: /dev/shm too small (1.2 GiB free))

# Pin a scratch filesystem instead (no fallback past the pin):
HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/scratch \
  ./andesim run my.elf --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 2047M
```

If you pin `HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/tmp` and `/tmp` is mounted as tmpfs (Arch
default), that does not lift the RAM ceiling; pick a directory on a
non-tmpfs filesystem (`/var/tmp`, `/scratch`, etc.) -- or just let the
tier list pick `~/.cache/andesim` for you.

The hardcoded `mktemp -p /dev/shm` paths in the shell harnesses
(`tests/e2e.sh`, `tests/drivers/*.sh`, `tests/plugin/*.sh`) all use
128 MiB and are unaffected.

### 2.5.1 Running on WSL2 and macOS

The hybrid handoff needs both legs (QEMU and vsim) on **one Linux
kernel**, with the mmap file on a filesystem local to that kernel.
That rule decides what each OS needs:

**Linux** -- native, nothing to do.

**Windows (WSL2)** -- works as Linux; two caveats:

- Keep the repo and the mmap dirs on the ext4 side (`~/...`), never
  under `/mnt/c` (drvfs is slow and `MAP_SHARED` is not coherent there).
- `/dev/shm` is capped by the WSL VM memory. Raise `memory=` in
  `%UserProfile%\.wslconfig` if tier 1 is too small -- or just let the
  tier list fall through to `~/.cache/andesim`.

`./andesim doctor` checks both (see the `mmap tiers:` section and the
WSL warnings at the end of its report).

**macOS** -- run-only. vsim is a Linux binary, so `./andesim` re-execs
the run inside a prebuilt Linux runtime image in the podman machine VM;
the mmap lives inside that VM (the container's `/dev/shm`), never on a
virtiofs mount. One-time setup:

```sh
brew install podman
podman machine init --memory 4096   # the VM hosts /dev/shm (tier 1)
podman machine start
podman pull <runtime image>         # or load a CI-built andesim-runtime:latest
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --mem-size 256M my.elf
```

Knobs: `ANDESIM_IMAGE` (image name, default `andesim-runtime:latest`),
`ANDESIM_SHM_SIZE` (container `/dev/shm`, default `3g`),
`ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE` (podman/docker). Your current directory is
bind-mounted at the same path, so relative ELF paths and output files
work; builds (`scripts/build_all.sh`) stay Linux-only. The image is built on
Linux from `Dockerfile.runtime` (it bakes a fully built repo at
`/opt/hybrid_sim`); Apple Silicon runs the x86-64 image under emulation,
so expect slower wall-clock than a Linux host.

### 2.6 The hybrid guest memory map (`--print-memmap`)

Which addresses may a hybrid workload touch? Print the map for exactly the
run you are about to do (same `--engine` / `--mem-size`; the ELF is optional
and only adds a fit note):

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --print-memmap --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 128M
```

```
REGION           BASE         END          SIZE    TRANSPORT
DRAM             0x0          0x7ffffff    128M    shared mmap; content survives the handoff
V-scratch        0x8000000    0x8000fff    4K      reserved by the hybrid V transport; not program-usable
ILM              0x0          0xffff       64K     sidecar .ilm; DRAM overlay while milmb.IEN=1
DLM              0x200000     0x207fff     32K     sidecar .dlm; DRAM overlay while mdlmb.IEN=1
HVM              0x90000000   0x9003ffff   256K    sidecar .hvm
SimControl/HTIF  0xe0080000   0xe0080fff   4K      device; state does not cross the handoff
UART2            0xf0300000   0xf03fffff   1M      device (console); state does not cross the handoff
```

Reading the table:

- **END is the inclusive last byte**; SIZE is the region span.
- **DRAM** tracks `--mem-size`; the **V-scratch** page above it belongs to
  the V-register transport (2.5) -- the driver rejects an ELF that reaches
  into it.
- **ILM/DLM/HVM** rows appear only when the engine can actually transport
  their content (`--describe` sizes > 0, the backdoor gate); their bases come
  from the engine's own `--print-qemu-config` geometry -- the same file the
  QEMU leg boots with -- so the printed map IS the run's effective one.
- **Devices**: only the vplat set both engines model is listed. Device STATE
  never crosses the handoff (each engine has its own UART/SimControl
  instance); only RAM content does.
- Anything NOT in the table is unsupported in hybrid mode: it is modeled by
  one engine only (QEMU's PLIC/PLMT/MROM/virtio..., vsim's debug-module
  window), so touching it inside the ROI gives engine-specific behavior.

The map is hybrid-only surface: `--mode fast|cycle` run one engine's native
map, which the driver does not model (`--print-memmap` errors there). vsim's
own `--print-memmap` dumps its interconnect routing table -- useful for
engine bring-up, but it is one engine's view, not the hybrid contract;
`tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_print_memmap.sh` cross-checks the two so they
cannot drift apart.

## 3. Switching modes - which trigger to use

| Mode     | Profiles          | Switch boundary                                          | Cycle figure           |
|----------|-------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|------------------------|
| marker   | a kernel          | `slti x0,x0,0x5A0/1` insn match (markers in source)         | kernel cycles          |
| PC       | a kernel          | PC equals a boundary: any symbol or `0x` address (both `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` required) | kernel cycles |

Marker/PC delimit ONE kernel you choose. Both go through `./andesim run
--mode hybrid --trigger marker|pc`. The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle`
delta.

Decision flow:

```
Profiling ONE region you can name (a kernel)?
  binary is yours to edit          -> marker (andesim_ROI_begin()/end() around it)
  not editable, symbol/PC at ends  -> PC   (./andesim run --mode hybrid
                                            --trigger pc --pc-start S --pc-end E)
```

**Hardware-config sync.** A hybrid run models ONE core on two engines, so
the QEMU fast leg inherits the selected engine's hardware config. Three
things flow from engine to QEMU, all derived from the engine's frozen
`config.inc`:

- **VLEN** comes from the engine's `--describe` (512 when the engine
  reports none) and shows in the run banner as `vlen=N`.
- **The ISA** (extensions: CoDense, Zfh, Zba/Zbb/Zbc/Zbs, `xandesv5isa`,
  ...) comes from the engine's `--print-qemu-config`: the driver captures
  that QEMU `-readconfig` cfg and hands it to the fast leg, so QEMU executes
  the same extensions the engine models instead of a fixed `-cpu` string.
  An engine built without the flag (an older binary) makes the driver fall
  back to its default `-cpu` with no error. See `docs/qemu_match_ROADMAP.md`.
- **ILM/DLM content** (`--describe` `ilm_size`/`dlm_size`, bytes): when the
  engine has local memories, the fast leg's plugin also drains their content
  into `<state>.ilm`/`.dlm` sidecar files and the vsim leg loads them back
  (`--ilm`/`--dlm`), so a program that stages code/data in TCM before the ROI
  resumes with that content in place. An engine without local memories (or an
  older binary that does not report them) adds nothing. A guest that uses TCM
  must enable it itself (write `milmb`/`mdlmb`) -- which real TCM firmware
  does anyway; that CSR write rides the v6 write-mask so the enable is
  restored on the vsim leg. See `ROADMAP_ilm_dlm.md`.
- **HVM content** (`--describe` `hvm_size`, bytes): same contract for the
  High-Bandwidth Vector Memory at `0x90000000` -- the plugin drains
  `<state>.hvm`, the vsim leg backdoor-loads it (`--hvm`), and the exit
  drain dumps it back next to the handoff-out state. A program that stages
  vector data in HVM before the ROI resumes with that data in place; there
  is no enable bit (the geometry CSRs `mhvm_cfg`/`mhvmb` are read-only
  constants both sides derive from the same config). See `ROADMAP_hvm.md`.

An engine whose XLEN is not 64 (e.g. `vsim:d23`, rv32) cannot share
architectural state with the rv64 fast leg and is rejected with a clear
error.

**Preview the commands (`--dry-run`).** Add `--dry-run` to **any** mode
(`fast`, `cycle`, or `hybrid`) to print the exact engine command line(s) --
fully resolved and shell-quoted, including any matched `-readconfig` and all
paths -- and run nothing. `fast`/`cycle` print their single standalone command;
`hybrid` prints both legs:

```
./andesim run --mode fast --dry-run prog.elf
# [andesim] dry-run: 1 command(s), not executed
# # command 1/1: standalone [qemu64]
# qemu-system-riscv64 -machine andes_ae350 -cpu andes-ax46mpv ... -bios prog.elf

./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --dry-run --engine vsim:<cfg> prog.elf
# [andesim] dry-run: 2 command(s), not executed
# # command 1/2: fast-leg [qemu64]
# qemu-system-riscv64 ... -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 ... -readconfig <tmp>/qemu.cfg
# # command 2/2: accurate-leg [vsim:<cfg>]
# sim_<cfg> prog.elf --resume-from-qemu <tmp>/state-0.bin --handoff-out ...
```

Supported VLEN range: 128 to 1024 bits. The handoff state file reserves
128 bytes per vector register (`HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX`); an engine whose
VLEN exceeds 1024 is refused with a clear error instead of silently
truncating the V registers. A standalone fast run defaults to the
vector-capable CPU `andes-ax46mpv` (rv64) / `andes-a46mpv` (rv32), so RVV
binaries run out of the box at the cpu model's built-in VLEN; andesim itself
passes no `vlen`. To pin an exact VLEN, add a `-cpu` through the passthrough
tail, e.g. `andesim run --mode fast app.elf -- -cpu andes-ax46mpv,vlen=256`
(the last `-cpu` wins).

Where `--` args land depends on the mode. `fast`/`cycle` forward them to their
single engine (qemu / vsim). `hybrid` has **two** legs (a QEMU fast-forward and
a vsim measure leg) whose command lines the driver builds itself, so there is no
single "the engine" to forward to -- `hybrid` therefore **rejects** `-- args`
(rc=2) rather than silently dropping them or guessing a leg. For vsim options use
the dedicated flags (`--kanata`/`--objdump`); to pin VLEN, pick the right
`--engine` (each vsim engine has a fixed VLEN).

**`cycle` output.** A `cycle` run prints just two things: the program's own
output, then the cycle count as andesim's own one-line result --

```
$ ./andesim run --mode cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium hello.elf
hello
[andesim] 3573 cycles
```

vsim's startup banner (the `Copyright ... / Version :` lines) and its verbose
`[info]` log are hidden so the result stands alone; real `[warn]`/`[error]`
diagnostics still pass through, and the engine exit code is propagated. (`fast`
is raw passthrough -- QEMU's output is shown verbatim, and QEMU prints no such
banner or cycle line. `cycle --gdb` is interactive and is not filtered.)

**Window boundary semantics.** Markers are HINT NOPs: the window is the
span strictly between them. A pc boundary is real user code: the
instruction at `--pc-start` executes
INSIDE the measured window -- the fast leg stops just before it and vsim
resumes at it, so no instruction is lost across the handoff. The
instruction at `--pc-end` is where vsim drains. `--pc-start` and `--pc-end`
must resolve to **different** addresses (compared numerically, so `main` and
its literal `0x..` address count as equal): an equal pair is an empty ROI --
vsim would drain the instant it resumes -- and is rejected up front with rc=2.

> **Writing a kernel for cycle measurement (marker/PC modes):** keep the measured
> kernel anchored inside the `slti x0,x0,0x5A0/1` span -- read its inputs and
> write its outputs through memory inside the span, or wrap the kernel in a
> `__attribute__((noinline))` function called between the markers. The
> markers' `"memory"` clobber pins memory I/O but not register-only compute,
> so a kernel that carries live vector values in registers across the
> boundary may be hoisted/sunk out of the measured window. See
> `tests/fixtures/runtime/rt_c_helpers.h`.

---

## 4. Walk-through: one handoff in each mode

Each section is copy-pastable. They all share the same setup.

### 4.0 Common setup (do once per shell)

```sh
cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim
source ./setup.sh                         # builds + exports env vars
make -C tests/fixtures -j        # builds .elf fixtures
```

Quick env check:

```sh
echo "$VSIM_QEMU"
echo "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
echo "$VSIM_BIN"
ls tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf
```

### 4.1 marker mode - the default (kernel)

Goal: run a vector fixture through QEMU1 -> vsim using the
two ROI markers (`slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1`) that the fixture already contains.

```sh
./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium
```

Expected output (stderr + stdout):

```
[andesim] model=hybrid engine=vsim:ax45mpv_premium vlen=<N> trigger=marker fixture=rt_c_v_matmul
[marker window_cycles] <N>  (vsim mcycle=<V> - qemu mcycle=<Q>)
PASS: --mode hybrid --trigger marker (rt_c_v_matmul)
```

The relayed output is just the program's own prints plus andesim's own lines:
vsim's startup banner (the `Copyright ... / Version :` lines) is stripped from
the vsim leg, the same as `cycle` mode, so the result stands alone. (vsim's
`[info]` log never reaches here -- the leg's stderr is dropped at capture.)

`./andesim run` orchestrates the two legs directly (no Python wrapper). Inside, the two legs are:

```
1) QEMU1 with -plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=$STATE
        -> drain at slti x0,x0,0x5A0   -> exit 200
2) sim_ax45mpv_premium $ELF \
        --resume-from-qemu $STATE --handoff-out $STATE_V \
        --shared-mem-path $SHM --shared-mem-size 128MB
        -> ROI runs in vsim, drains at slti x0,x0,0x5A1   -> exit 200
```

Try a different fixture:

```sh
./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_matmul.elf --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium
```

### 4.2 PC mode - markerless workload, explicit boundary PCs

Same plumbing as marker mode, but the binary carries **no** trigger markers.
The user picks the switch PCs explicitly via `--pc-start` and `--pc-end`,
each a symbol name or `0x` address. Both args are required for `--mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium`.

Don't know where the hot region is? `build/hotloops` runs the binary
fast and reports the hottest loops (function, source line, PC range) as
an LLM-ready Markdown fact sheet. It auto-detects the QEMU binary,
plugin, and CPU from your build. Each loop block carries a `measure:`
field — a ready `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` pair that covers the enclosing
function entry to `ret` — that pastes straight into the command above.
`docs/andes_sim_gemm_tutorial.ipynb` walks that workflow end to end.

```sh
./build/hotloops --min-iters 10 my_kernel.elf
```

```sh
# resolve the boundary PCs once (cheap, host-side; needs HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ELF=tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf
START=vmatmul_kernel
END=$(${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN}/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump -d "$ELF" \
        | awk '/<main>:/{flag=1} flag&&/jal[[:space:]]+.*<vmatmul_kernel>/{getline; print "0x"$1; exit}' \
        | tr -d ':')

./andesim run "$ELF" --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --pc-start "$START" --pc-end "$END"
```

`rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf` is the **markerless twin** of the GEMM fixture,
built `-DHYBRID_MARKERLESS` from the same source as the marked
`rt_c_v_matmul`. Both triggers are one-shot (QEMU plugin `exit(200)` on
first match; vsim drains on first match), so the measured window is
**exactly one full `vmatmul_kernel` call** (16 outer rows + inner k-loop
+ vse32 stores). The cycle count should land near marker mode's ~22808.

The mechanism is fully general - pc mode can target **any** symbol or raw
address. `./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium` resolves `--pc-start` / `--pc-end` directly (symbol name or `0x` address) without needing env vars.

The underlying QEMU and vsim invocations (what the driver orchestrates):

```sh
# Resolve the boundaries (objdump-based; pick any two PCs in the ELF):
OBJDUMP=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump
NM=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm
ROI_START=$("$NM" tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
              | awk '$3=="vmatmul_kernel"{print "0x"$1}')
ROI_END=$("$OBJDUMP" -d tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
              | awk '/<main>:/{flag=1} flag&&/jal[[:space:]]+.*<vmatmul_kernel>/{getline; print "0x"$1; exit}' \
              | tr -d ':')
echo "enter=$ROI_START  exit=$ROI_END"   # e.g. 0x10021c / 0x1002cc

# QEMU1 leg
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=/dev/shm/share,size=134217728 \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -bios tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=/tmp/q1.bin,enter_pc=$ROI_START"

# vsim leg
"$VSIM_BIN" tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
  --resume-from-qemu /tmp/q1.bin \
  --handoff-out /tmp/v.bin \
  --shared-mem-path /dev/shm/share \
  --shared-mem-size 134217728 \
  --hybrid-exit-pc "$ROI_END"
```

The fixture binary differs from marker mode (markerless vs marked), and the
QEMU1 plugin and vsim flags carry hex PCs (`enter_pc=` / `--hybrid-exit-pc`)
instead of marker-trigger plumbing.

### 4.3 Capturing a Kanata pipeline trace of the ROI

When debugging a hot path on vsim, pass `--kanata FILE` to `./andesim run`
in marker or pc mode. The resulting trace contains pipeline records only
for the ROI region (between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain) -- vsim
boot and DMI resume overhead are filtered out.

```sh
# marker mode: the ROI is the span between the two ROI markers (slti x0,x0,0x5A0/1)
# markers already in the source. vsim auto-derives the window.
./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf \
  --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --kanata /tmp/roi.kanata

# pc mode: the ROI bounds are whatever PCs you passed.
./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
  --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --pc-start vmatmul_kernel --pc-end 0x1002cc \
  --kanata /tmp/roi.kanata
```

Add `--objdump FILE` so the kanata `L` records embed the disassembly
text next to each PC. Generate the dump once with the toolchain
`objdump -d`:

```sh
$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump -d \
  tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf > /tmp/roi.S
./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf \
  --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --kanata /tmp/roi.kanata --objdump /tmp/roi.S
```

Open `/tmp/roi.kanata` in [Konata](https://github.com/shioyadan/Konata)
to view the pipeline.

Constraints:

- `--kanata` is only valid with `--mode hybrid --trigger marker` or `--mode hybrid --trigger pc` (the only triggers with a single ROI-exit PC); any other trigger is rejected with rc=2.
- marker mode requires exactly one `slti x0,x0,0x5A1` (exit marker) in the
  ELF. If the binary has more than one, vsim errors out with
  `multiple ... markers in ELF -- use \`--mode hybrid --trigger pc\` with explicit \`--pc-end\``.
  Switch to pc mode and pick the desired exit explicitly.
- `--objdump` requires `--kanata`.

How it works:

- `./andesim` appends `--kanata FILE --kanata-roi`
  (and `--objdump FILE`) to vsim's argv.
- vsim's `--kanata-roi` flag defers the kanata enable until after
  `--resume-from-qemu` loads the input state and `enable_hybrid_handoff`
  scans the ELF, then derives a one-shot `LoopGate`:
  - `start_pc` = the resumed PC (where vsim first fetches user code)
  - `end_pc`   = `--hybrid-exit-pc` (pc mode) or the unique
    `slti x0,x0,0x5A1` PC from CsrTrigger (marker mode)
  - `skip_iters=0`, `record_iters=1` (open on first fetch of start_pc,
    close on first retire of end_pc).

### 4.4 Verifying a hybrid run against a QEMU oracle (`--verify`)

With the QEMU2 handback removed, the code after your ROI never runs, so a
hybrid run normally proves only that a cycle figure came out. `--verify`
(default OFF) cross-checks the run's correctness:

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --verify your_prog.elf
# ...
# [marker window_cycles] 46  (vsim mcycle=... - qemu mcycle=...)
# [state-diff] PASS: 109 fields match (counters and passthrough CSRs excluded)
# [verify] PASS: vsim drain matches the QEMU oracle
```

Performance note: without `--verify`, the vsim leg drains only `mcycle`/`minstret`
(the cycle figure) and skips reading back the full architectural register file
over the Debug Module. A full drain reads every GPR, FPR, and transported CSR
with one Abstract Command each (only the vector registers ride a Program-Buffer
sweep through the shared scratch page); those simulated debug cycles dominate
hybrid wall-clock for a short ROI but never affect the cycle count -- the
counters are read before the rest of the drain. `--verify` needs every field
for the diff, so it keeps the full drain; expect a `--verify` run to take
noticeably longer than the same run without it.

How it works: after the normal run, the same ELF re-runs on pure QEMU (the
oracle) with the plugin draining at the ROI exit boundary, sampled at the
exact pc where vsim halted. The pre-ROI path is QEMU in both runs, so the
ROI inputs are identical -- any architectural divergence inside the ROI
(RTL bug, state-restore bug, drain bug) shows up as a field mismatch and
the run exits non-zero, listing each differing field:

```
[state-diff] x10: ref=0x3d got=0x0
[state-diff] FAIL: 1 mismatch(es) (115 fields compared)
```

What is compared: pc, all GPRs, all FPRs (when FP state is live), the V
CSRs and full vector registers (when V state is live), and the writable
M-mode CSRs that round-trip through the handoff -- `mscratch` (L23) and
`mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie` (L24), restored at resume and re-read at
drain. What is not:

- `mcycle`/`minstret` -- the engines count differently by design;
- `mip` -- restored and re-read, but its pending bits are hardware-driven
  (the timer bit tracks elapsed time, which differs between QEMU's
  functional clock and vsim's cycle clock), so a compare would
  false-positive;
- `mstatus`, `mtvec` -- passthrough: vsim restores the QEMU1 entry snapshot value; both sides hold the same bits by construction so comparing is trivially true but not useful;
- `satp`, `medeleg`/`mideleg` -- S-mode CSRs, not implemented on the default M-only engine. The privilege level itself IS compared: both
  sides drain the real one (L6), so a wrong-privilege resume shows up as
  a priv mismatch.

The handoff also carries the **v6 write-mask**: the plugin tracks which config
CSRs (the Andes block, PMA, the M-ext block, `mcache_ctl`/`mmisc_ctl`) your
program actually WROTE, and the cycle engine restores -- and `--verify`
compares -- only those. A CSR the program never touched keeps the engine's own
reset value instead of inheriting QEMU's reset default, so reset-value
differences between QEMU and any engine cannot skew the run. The tracking is
translation-time work in the plugin (only CSR-write instructions get a
callback), so the fast leg's speed is unaffected.

The write-mask also powers an **incompatibility warning** on every hybrid run
(not just `--verify`): if your program wrote a config CSR the chosen cycle
engine does not implement, the driver prints

```
[andesim] warning: the program wrote CSRs engine vsim:<engine> does not
implement: <names> (on this engine's silicon these writes would trap; the
hybrid restore skipped them)
```

to stderr. On that engine's real silicon the `csrw` would trap before the ROI,
so the cycle figure may not represent this program on this engine -- pick an
engine that implements those CSRs, or drop the writes. A clean run prints
nothing.

The handoff also carries the **v5 L2C block**: the L2 cache controller's MMIO
register window (0x0000..0x0527, base 0xE0500000). This is device MMIO, not a
CSR -- the QEMU plugin reads the window by physical address, and vsim writes back
only the writable boot-static config registers (Control 0x0008 = `CEN` enable +
prefetch + ECC + RAM timing, HPM Control, Way Allocation Masks) via
Program-Buffer stores before resuming. It is the L2 analog of the L1 `mcache_ctl`
transport and matters for the cycle figure the same way: an L2-enabled engine
that resumed with L2 disabled would run the ROI severalfold slower. Restore is
gated on the cycle engine actually having an L2C (`NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB > 0`);
every engine shipped today is built without one, so the block rides
forward-looking and no-ops. `--verify` compares the Control Register (masking the
read-only INITSTATUS bit).

The handoff also carries the v3 Andes block (`mxstatus`, ILM/DLM bases, PMA, ...)
and the **v4 M-ext block** (`HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST`): the writable M-mode CSRs
across the whole AndeStar V5 SPA -- perf counters, NMI, CLIC, trap-save,
state-enable, debug triggers, ePMP, CCTL, peripheral bases, U-mode Andes control
(51 CSRs). Every one is **capability-gated by CSR address**: an engine restores,
drains, and `--verify`-compares only the CSRs its config implements (reported via
`--describe andes_csrs`), so a CSR the core lacks is a no-op rather than a DM
hang. On the default `ax45mpv_premium` (M-only) that gates on the perf-monitor +
trigger CSRs; the rest ride forward-looking for a CLIC / Smrnmi / Smstateen /
M+U-capable engine. A few supported-but-engine-divergent CSRs are transported and
restored but excluded from `--verify` (like `msp_bound`): the HW perf counters
`mhpmcounter3-6`, `mdcause`, the trigger defaults `tdata1`/`tcontrol`, and the
ILM/DLM base+enable CSRs `milmb`/`mdlmb` (their enable bit reads 1 on the vsim
RTL but 0 on QEMU, which models no local memory). The
complete per-CSR disposition for all 232 spec CSRs is in
`docs/csr_coverage.ipynb`, guarded against drift by
`tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py`.

Per-engine CSR validation is a registration requirement: every supported
engine build carries its own CSR manifest + registration report under
`tests/engines/` (contract: `tests/engines/README.md`). For a human-readable
answer to "which CSRs does this engine restore, and under which condition --
or why not", read the engine's `csr_restore_table.md` in the same directory
(generated from the manifest by `tests/engines/render_restore_table.py`;
`test_restore_table.sh` guards it against drift).
`docs/engine_registration_tutorial.ipynb` walks the whole lifecycle --
the three-way audit (spec x config.inc x RTL), registering a new engine or
config, and removing one. `docs/csr_transport_bringup_tutorial.ipynb` is the
companion reference: what the `/csr-transport-bringup` skill does (its 7-phase
pipeline), every column of `csr_manifest.csv`, and each file a registration
ships under `tests/engines/<engine>-<confighash>/`.

Costs and limits: the oracle leg is one extra QEMU run of the whole
program (MHz-class -- cheap next to the vsim leg). `--verify` works with
`--trigger marker|pc`, assumes the single-shot ROI the hybrid run itself
assumes, and requires `--mode hybrid` (the other models have nothing to
cross-check).

1028	engines model at the same addresses, so ONE ELF runs on `fast`, on `cycle`,
1029	and across a `hybrid` handoff, and a syscall inside the ROI works (it just
1030	adds its real cycles to the figure). Every in-tree C fixture links this
1031	runtime; nothing in the repo uses `-lgloss_vh` anymore.

1040	(`scripts/build_all.sh runtime`, or any fixture build does it implicitly),

### 4.5 Debugging with GDB (`--gdb`, `--gdb-port`)

Add `--gdb` to attach a debugger to a running simulation.

**fast model** -- starts QEMU's built-in GDB stub and pauses at the entry point:
```sh
./andesim run --mode fast --gdb my.elf
# In another terminal:
gdb-multiarch -ex 'target remote :1234' my.elf
```

-- your JTAG debug server -- in the foreground:
```sh

./andesim run --mode cycle --gdb --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium my.elf
# then point GDB at the server's gdb port (OpenOCD's default is 1111):
gdb-multiarch -ex 'target remote :1111' my.elf
```

connects to the **server's own** gdb port, not this one. The hart starts halted,
so the debugger attaches to a stopped core -- set breakpoints, then `continue`.

`<cfg>` selects `adapter driver remote_bitbang` at `remote_bitbang port 9104`,
a generic `riscv` target, and a `gdb_port`. A full worked example is in
`docs/andes_sim_demo.ipynb` ("7. Debug with GDB"). **Note:** Andes ICEman's
*own* bundled OpenOCD 0.10 has a `remote_bitbang` bug that crashes against vsim's
DTM, so point `$ICEMAN` at a modern OpenOCD rather than the bundled one.

| `cannot resolve ROI start/end '<x>'`                   | PC-mode boundary `<x>` is neither a `0x` address nor a defined symbol. Fix `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` (or `ROI_START`/`ROI_END`), or use marker mode. |
| Whole suite times out under `scripts/run_e2e.sh`               | Set `JOBS=8`. Default 128 saturates a 128-core host.                 |
| `[FAIL] [N/M] ... -> /tmp/e2e-XXXX/...log`             | Open that log; it is the full stdout+stderr of the failing leg.      |

---

## 8. Where to go next

- `docs/andes_sim_demo.ipynb` - 5-minute product demo: one `hello` ELF
  on fast, cycle and hybrid, with ROI markers around a single `printf`
  and a no-source-edit `--trigger pc` run on objdump-found addresses.
- `docs/andes_sim_options_tutorial.ipynb` - the `andesim run` option
  reference: every flag (`--mode`, `--engine`, `--trigger`/`--pc-*`,
  `--mem-size`, `--dry-run`, `--verify`, `--gdb`, passthrough `--`) with
  one live demo each, plus an error gallery (missing ELF, rv32/rv64
  mismatch, omitted required flags) showing the exact message and fix.
- `docs/andes_sim_gemm_tutorial.ipynb` - measure a real RVV GEMM kernel:
  build + verify against plain C, read engine hardware params
  (XLEN/VLEN/DLEN/ELEN), kernel cycles via markers, then the no-edit
  path: `build/hotloops` detector -> `--trigger pc` on the hot function.
- `docs/andes_sim_memory_tutorial.ipynb` - guest memory: a program that
  needs nearly 2 GiB faults under the default and passes with the hybrid
  ceiling `--mem-size 2047M` (exactly 2G is rejected -- the V-scratch page
  would overflow the window); per-model semantics, the cap, backing-store
  tiers, doctor's
  `mmap tiers:` readout, WSL2/macOS notes.
- `docs/andes_sim_limitations.ipynb` - what the simulator CANNOT do today:
  the narrow ROI envelope (trap-free, no paging; M/S/U privilege is
  transported since L6 was resolved, but the ROI must hold one privilege
  and the engine's RTL must implement it -- M-mode-only engines abort
  loudly on an S/U handoff), the full L1-L21 list with live evidence
  cells, and the commercial-readiness scorecard.
- `docs/competition_landscape.ipynb` - where andesim sits against
  Dromajo, ImperasDV (Synopsys) and gem5: a positioning map plus
  capability/dimension tables across cosim, fast-forward, accuracy,
  speed, cost, interrupts/exceptions, OS boot and RVVI support, plus a
  "which one should I use" guide. andesim is the
  only one pairing functional fast-forward with cycle-accuracy from the
  real RTL; the others are functional golden models (Dromajo, ImperasDV)
  or a cycle-approximate performance model (gem5).
- `docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md` - one exercise per mode with
  drill-down on the underlying CLI invocations.
- `CLAUDE.md` - file-level pointers (key files, build commands,
  fixture authoring rules).
- `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.c` - the RVV GEMM the switching modes
  run; one source builds both the marked (marker mode) and markerless
  (pc mode) variants.
- `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_regs.c` - reference fixture for V-regfile transport
  (V regfile + V scalar CSRs + shared memory).

# Commit Refactor Plan (for review)

## What I will do (all 3 repos)

1. **Reset** all Nick Hung commits on the feature branch. Originals are kept safe under
   `backup/andesim-pre-refactor` and `backup/qemu-isa-match-pre-refactor` (nothing is lost).
2. **Rebuild** the entire diff as small commits, **organized by functionality**.
3. Each functionality is **prototype-first**:
   - a **minimal** commit = the smallest real working slice (e.g. transport only `f0`), **with its test in the same commit**;
   - a **complete** commit = fill in the rest (`f1..f31`), **with its test in the same commit**.
   - A genuinely atomic change (one fix / one doc / one removal) stays **one** commit.
4. **Remove all unneeded legacy code** (see "Removed for good" per repo).
5. The **final tree is unchanged** vs today's tip, except the legacy that is deleted. So the code still
   builds and all tests still pass at the end; only the *history* changes.

`(min)` = minimal prototype, `(done)` = completion. `ABI vN` = advances the shared-ABI submodule pin.

usage: andesim <command> [options] <ELF> [-- <engine args>]

Multi-engine driver for the Andes simulators (QEMU + vsim).

run     run one simulation
  fast      QEMU only -- functional, full speed
  cycle     one cycle-accurate engine, from reset
  hybrid    QEMU fast-forwards, then vsim measures the ROI

  --mode fast|cycle|hybrid    REQUIRED  which mode to run
  --trigger marker|pc         REQUIRED for hybrid  the ROI delimiter
    --pc-start <sym|0x>       REQUIRED for --trigger pc  ROI start boundary
    --pc-end <sym|0x>         REQUIRED for --trigger pc  ROI end boundary
  --engine <id>               pick an engine, e.g. vsim:ax45mpv_premium (default: the sole one)
  --mem-size <spec>           guest RAM, e.g. 256M / 2G (hybrid: max 2G; fast: QEMU -m; cycle: ignored)
  --dry-run                   print the exact engine command(s) and exit, running nothing (fast/cycle/hybrid)
  --print-memmap              print the hybrid guest memory map and exit, running nothing (hybrid only; ELF optional)
  --verify                    cross-check the hybrid run against a QEMU oracle
  --gdb                       pause at startup for a debugger (fast: QEMU stub; cycle: vsim JTAG + $ICEMAN; not hybrid)
  --gdb-port <port>           override the --gdb port (fast 1234, cycle 9104)
  -- <args...>                forward everything after -- verbatim to the engine (fast/cycle only; hybrid rejects -- args)

list    list what is available
  models    the modes and their engines
  engines   discovered cycle-accurate engines

doctor  check toolchain + fixtures are present

'andesim run --help' / 'andesim list --help' for per-command detail.

present, you get RVV-only filtering and per-loop disassembly context.

# --trigger menu offers only the supported triggers (marker|pc).

no_word "$RH" || fail "run --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has ' --mem-size' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --mem-size:"$'\n'"$RH"

has '^  --gdb '      "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb:"$'\n'"$RH"

has '^  --trigger ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --trigger:"$'\n'"$RH"

Armed by the engine's `--describe` sizes (`ilm_size`/`dlm_size`/`hvm_size`, bytes; 0 = no memory or wrapper lacks the set_*/get_* backdoor pair -- capability-gated so a config-has-it/wrapper-can't engine arms nothing). These QEMU memories are per-CPU overlays (LM) or standalone RAM (HVM), NOT backed by the shared mmap, so the sidecars are the only road their content travels; QEMU's raw geometry must be synced (`-readconfig` on the driver path, `-global` in tests/e2e.sh -- HVM's property is `hvm_size_pow_2`, log2) because QEMU's compiled-in defaults (2 MB ILM at 0x0, 1-BYTE HVM) are wrong for every engine.

# andesim User Guide

Audience: an engineer who wants to RUN programs on the Andes simulators
through `./andesim` and measure cycle counts. This guide covers every
user-facing option and feature.

It assumes andesim and its engines are already installed and built
(QEMU, the vsim engines, the plugin, the runtime, and the test ELFs are
prebuilt). If something is missing, run `./andesim doctor` and hand the
report to whoever owns your install; building is covered in `README.md`,
not here.

---

## 1. What andesim is

andesim runs one RISC-V ELF on one of three models:

| Model    | What runs                              | Speed          | You get                    |
|----------|----------------------------------------|----------------|-----------------------------|
| `fast`   | QEMU only (functional)                 | MHz-class      | program output, fast        |
| `cycle`  | one cycle-accurate engine, from reset  | kHz-class      | program output + total cycles |
| `hybrid` | QEMU fast-forwards, then the cycle engine measures one region you choose | fast until your region | program output + cycles of JUST your region |

`hybrid` is the headline feature: QEMU races through boot and setup, then
hands the complete architectural state and memory to the cycle-accurate
engine (vsim, built from the real RTL), which runs only your
region-of-interest (ROI). The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta
across that window. You mark the window with a **trigger**: source-level
markers or a pair of PCs (section 5.3).

One run models ONE core. The cycle engine defines the hardware (ISA,
VLEN, caches); in hybrid mode the QEMU leg automatically inherits that
engine's ISA and VLEN so both legs execute the same architecture.

---

## 2. Check your installation

```sh
./andesim doctor          # read-only health report
./andesim list models     # the three models
./andesim list engines    # every engine you can pass to --engine
```

`doctor` checks artifacts, toolchain, runtime, engines, and the shared-memory
backing tiers, and prints WSL2 advice where relevant. A healthy install ends
with `Summary: N PASS, 0 FAIL`.

`list engines` shows what `--engine` accepts:

```
ENGINE                 TYPE  KIND            XLEN  VLEN  DLEN  ELEN
qemu64                 qemu  functional      64    -     -     -
qemu32                 qemu  functional      32    -     -     -
vsim:ax45mpv_premium   vsim  cycle-accurate  64    512   512   32
vsim:ax46mpv_advanced  vsim  cycle-accurate  64    512   512   32
```

`qemu64`/`qemu32` are the functional engines (`fast`); the `vsim:<cfg>`
entries are the cycle-accurate engines (`cycle`, and the measuring leg of
`hybrid`). `-` means the engine does not report that parameter.

Run `./andesim run -h` any time for the compact flag list; this guide is
the long version.

---

## 3. First runs

The install ships ready-made ELFs under `tests/fixtures/`; the examples
below use them. Replace with your own ELF once you have one (section 4).

### 3.1 fast -- functional, full speed

```sh
./andesim run --mode fast tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf
```

```
hello from vplat
```

Output is the program's own output, verbatim (QEMU passthrough). The exit
code of your program becomes the process exit code.

### 3.2 cycle -- one engine, from reset, total cycles

```sh
./andesim run --mode cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf
```

```
hello from vplat
[andesim] 4247 cycles
```

The engine's startup banner and verbose info log are filtered out so the
result stands alone; real warnings/errors still pass through, and the
program's exit code is propagated. The figure is the whole run from reset
-- boot, runtime init, everything.

### 3.3 hybrid -- fast-forward, then measure your region

`hybrid` needs a trigger that says where the measured window starts and
ends. The fixture below already contains ROI markers, so `--trigger
marker` works out of the box:

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
  tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf
```

```
[andesim] model=hybrid engine=vsim:ax45mpv_premium vlen=512 trigger=marker fixture=rt_c_hello
[hsim mmap] 128.0 MiB at /dev/shm (free: 251.5 GiB)
hello from QEMU1
[marker window_cycles] 54  (vsim mcycle=... - qemu mcycle=...)
PASS: --mode hybrid --trigger marker (rt_c_hello)
```

Reading the output:

- The banner names the resolved engine, its VLEN, and the trigger.
- `[hsim mmap]` names the shared-memory file backing the run (section 5.4).
- `hello from QEMU1` is the program's own output from the fast leg.
- `[marker window_cycles] 54` is the answer: your ROI took 54 cycles on
  this engine. It is the vsim `mcycle` delta across the window.
- The run ends after the ROI. Code after your ROI never executes in a
  hybrid run -- hybrid is a measuring tool, not a way to finish the program.

The first hybrid run of a given (engine, ELF) pair is a few seconds slower:
andesim captures the engine's reset state once and caches it under
`~/.cache/andesim/` so later runs can skip restoring registers that still
hold reset values (typically ~4x faster on the vsim leg). The cache
refreshes itself when the engine or the ELF changes.

---

## 4. Prepare your own program

### 4.1 Compile once, run on every engine

Link against the andesim runtime and one ELF runs on `fast`, on `cycle`,
and across a `hybrid` handoff -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting:

```sh
riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O2 \
  -B <andesim>/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
```

- Use your Andes RISC-V GCC (the one `./andesim doctor` reports).
- `-B` points gcc at the runtime artifacts; use the absolute path when
  compiling outside the repo.
- `-specs=andesim.specs` swaps in the runtime's `crt0.o`, links
  `andesim.ld` (load base `0x00100000`), and pins the library order, so no
  semihosting library can leak into the link.
- Add `v` to `-march` (e.g. `rv64gcv`) for RVV code.

For rv32 targets use the rv32 compiler and the rv32 runtime flavor:

```sh
riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O2 \
  -B <andesim>/build/runtime/rv32 -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
```

Custom build system (no gcc driver)? Link the pieces directly:

```sh
... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T build/runtime/andesim.ld \
  build/runtime/crt0.o your_prog.o -L build/runtime \
  -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
```

What the runtime gives your program, on every engine:

| Channel          | Behavior                                                       |
|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| stdio (fd 0-2)   | `printf` etc. go to the simulator console (a modeled UART)     |
| exit code        | `exit(n)` (n < 256) terminates the simulation; `n` becomes the simulator process exit code |
| file io (fd > 2) | `open`/`read`/`write` pass through to host files, resolved against the engine's working directory |

A `printf` inside a measured ROI works -- but it adds the real UART cycles
to your figure. Keep measured kernels I/O-free when you want clean numbers.

### 4.2 Mark your region (ROI markers)

For `--trigger marker`, wrap the region you want to measure:

```c
#include <andesim/ROI.h>   /* shipped with the runtime; rides the -B flag */

andesim_ROI_begin();
my_kernel(a, b, c);
andesim_ROI_end();
```

The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (architectural NOPs), so a marker
binary also runs unchanged on `fast`, on `cycle`, and on real silicon.
Ship one binary; measure when you want.

> **Measurement hygiene:** keep the kernel anchored inside the marker span
> -- read its inputs and write its outputs through memory inside the span,
> or wrap the kernel in a `__attribute__((noinline))` function called
> between the markers. The markers pin memory I/O but not register-only
> compute, so a kernel that carries live values in registers across the
> boundary may be hoisted or sunk out of the measured window by the
> compiler.

### 4.3 Cannot edit the binary? Use PC boundaries

`--trigger pc` needs no markers: you name the window with `--pc-start` and
`--pc-end`, each a symbol name or a `0x` address (section 5.3). To find
the hot region of an unknown binary first, run the bundled detector:

```sh
./build/hotloops --min-iters 10 my_kernel.elf
```

It runs the binary fast and reports the hottest loops (function, source
line, PC range) with a ready `measure:` line -- a `--pc-start`/`--pc-end`
pair you can paste straight into the hybrid command. See `docs/hotloops.md`
for the full flag reference.

---

## 5. The `run` options, one by one

Synopsis:

```
./andesim run --mode fast|cycle|hybrid [options] <ELF> [-- <engine args>]
```

### 5.1 `--mode fast|cycle|hybrid` (required)

Picks the model (section 1). Everything else keys off this choice.

### 5.2 `--engine <id>`

Picks the engine from `./andesim list engines`.

- `fast`: optional. The driver auto-selects `qemu64` or `qemu32` to match
  your ELF's width; an explicit `--engine qemu32|qemu64` overrides (with a
  warning if it disagrees with the ELF).
- `cycle` / `hybrid`: names the cycle-accurate engine. Optional only when
  exactly one is installed; with several you must choose:

  ```
  andesim run --mode cycle: model cycle: multiple cycle-accurate engines;
  select one with --engine (have: vsim:ax45mpv_premium, vsim:ax46mpv_advanced)
  ```

Width rules: `cycle`/`hybrid` reject an ELF whose width does not match the
engine, up front:

```
andesim run --mode cycle: ELF is rv32 but engine 'vsim:ax45mpv_premium' is rv64
  -- pick a matching engine or an rv64 ELF
```

Hybrid additionally requires an rv64 engine (the fast leg is rv64; an rv32
engine cannot share architectural state with it and is rejected).

VLEN: each vsim engine has a fixed VLEN (see `list engines`); in hybrid
mode the QEMU leg inherits the engine's ISA and VLEN automatically, so
both legs execute identical architecture. Supported VLEN range in hybrid:
128 to 1024 bits. A standalone `fast` run defaults to the vector-capable
`andes-ax46mpv` (rv64) / `andes-a46mpv` (rv32) CPU model; to pin an exact
VLEN there, append a `-cpu` through the passthrough tail (the last `-cpu`
wins):

```sh
./andesim run --mode fast app.elf -- -cpu andes-ax46mpv,vlen=256
```

### 5.3 `--trigger marker|pc` (+ `--pc-start`, `--pc-end`) -- hybrid only, required

The ROI delimiter for `--mode hybrid`.

**`--trigger marker`** (recommended when you can edit the source): the
window is the span strictly between `andesim_ROI_begin()` and
`andesim_ROI_end()` (section 4.2). The markers themselves are NOPs and
cost nothing.

**`--trigger pc`**: explicit boundaries, no source edits. Both flags are
required; each accepts a symbol name or a `0x` hex address:

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
  --pc-start vmatmul_kernel --pc-end 0x1002cc my.elf
```

Semantics you should know:

- The instruction at `--pc-start` executes INSIDE the measured window (the
  fast leg stops just before it; the cycle engine resumes at it -- no
  instruction is lost across the handoff). `--pc-end` is where the window
  closes.
- Symbols are resolved from the ELF's own symbol table by the driver; no
  toolchain is needed at run time. A name that is not defined fails with
  `symbol '<x>' not defined in <elf>`; a bad literal fails with
  `malformed address '<x>'`.
- Both triggers are one-shot: the first hit of the start boundary opens the
  window, the first hit of the end boundary closes it. For a function called
  many times, the window is the FIRST call.
- Start and end must resolve to different addresses; an equal pair is an
  empty window and is rejected up front:
  `--pc-start and --pc-end resolve to the same address 0x... (an empty ROI measures nothing)`.

### 5.4 `--mem-size <spec>` -- guest memory

`SPEC` accepts `256M`, `1.5G`, `2G`, or raw bytes. Per-model meaning:

| Model    | Effect |
|----------|--------|
| `hybrid` | Your program RAM (default `128M`). Max `2G` minus 4 KiB: the driver reserves one page just above your RAM for the vector-register transport, so exactly `2G` is rejected (use `2047M`) and an ELF whose static image reaches into the reserved page is rejected with `raise --mem-size or shrink the image`. |
| `fast`   | Forwarded as a plain QEMU `-m`. No 2G cap; QEMU validates the size itself. |
| `cycle`  | Ignored (the engine always models its full DRAM window); the driver says so on stderr. |

Where the hybrid shared memory lives: andesim allocates a file both legs
map. It picks the first tier with enough free space (request + 256 MiB
headroom) and always tells you which:

1. `/dev/shm` -- RAM-backed, fastest.
2. `~/.cache/andesim` -- disk-backed fallback (honors `XDG_CACHE_HOME`).

```
[hsim mmap] 2.0 GiB at /home/u/.cache/andesim (free: 2.1 TiB) (fallback: /dev/shm too small (1.2 GiB free))
```

Set `HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/path` to pin one directory with NO fallback past it
(the run fails with a hint if it cannot hold the request). Do not pin a
tmpfs mount (`/tmp` on some distros) expecting a disk ceiling -- tmpfs is
still RAM.

### 5.5 `--print-memmap` -- which addresses may a hybrid workload touch?

Prints the guest memory map for exactly the run you are about to do (same
`--engine`/`--mem-size`; the ELF is optional and only adds a fit note),
then exits without running anything. Hybrid only.

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --print-memmap --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 128M
```

```
[andesim] hybrid memory map: engine=vsim:ax45mpv_premium mem-size=128M
REGION           BASE         END          SIZE    TRANSPORT
DRAM             0x0          0x7ffffff    128M    shared mmap; content survives the handoff
V-scratch        0x8000000    0x8000fff    4K      reserved by the hybrid V transport; not program-usable
ILM              0x0          0xffff       64K     sidecar .ilm; DRAM overlay while milmb.IEN=1
DLM              0x200000     0x207fff     32K     sidecar .dlm; DRAM overlay while mdlmb.IEN=1
HVM              0x90000000   0x9003ffff   256K    sidecar .hvm
SimControl/HTIF  0xe0080000   0xe0080fff   4K      device; state does not cross the handoff
UART2            0xf0300000   0xf03fffff   1M      device (console); state does not cross the handoff
```

How to read it:

- END is the inclusive last byte.
- DRAM tracks `--mem-size`; the V-scratch page above it belongs to andesim.
- ILM/DLM/HVM rows appear only when the chosen engine has those memories
  and can transport their content; the addresses are the engine's own.
- Device state never crosses the handoff (each engine has its own UART and
  SimControl instance); only RAM content does.
- Anything NOT listed is unsupported in hybrid mode: it exists in one
  engine only, so touching it inside the ROI gives engine-specific behavior.

### 5.6 `--dry-run` -- preview without running

Valid in every mode: prints the exact engine command line(s), fully
resolved and shell-quoted, and runs nothing. `fast`/`cycle` print one
command; `hybrid` prints both legs. Use it to see precisely what a run
will execute, or to lift the command for your own scripting.

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --dry-run my.elf
# [andesim] dry-run: 2 command(s), not executed
# # command 1/2: fast-leg [qemu64]
# qemu-system-riscv64 ... -plugin .../libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=...
# # command 2/2: accurate-leg [vsim:ax45mpv_premium]
# sim_ax45mpv_premium my.elf --resume-from-qemu ... --handoff-out ...
```

### 5.7 `--verify` -- cross-check a hybrid run against a QEMU oracle

A hybrid run normally proves only that a cycle figure came out. `--verify`
(hybrid only, default off) re-runs the same ELF on pure QEMU up to the ROI
exit and compares the architectural state field by field against what the
cycle engine drained:

```
[marker window_cycles] 46  (vsim mcycle=... - qemu mcycle=...)
[state-diff] PASS: 109 fields match (counters and passthrough CSRs excluded)
[verify] PASS: vsim drain matches the QEMU oracle
```

A mismatch lists each differing field and exits non-zero:

```
[state-diff] x10: ref=0x3d got=0x0
[state-diff] FAIL: 1 mismatch(es) (115 fields compared)
```

What is compared: the PC, all GPRs, FPRs (when FP state is live), the
vector registers and V CSRs (when V is live), the privilege level, and the
M-mode CSRs that round-trip through the handoff. Deliberately excluded:
`mcycle`/`minstret` (the engines count differently by design), `mip`
(hardware-driven pending bits), and a few CSRs whose reset values
legitimately differ between engines.

Two costs: one extra QEMU run of the whole program (cheap), and a full
register read-back over the Debug Module at the ROI exit (not cheap --
without `--verify` the exit drain reads only the two counters). Expect a
`--verify` run to take noticeably longer; the cycle figure itself is not
affected.

Related, printed on EVERY hybrid run (not just `--verify`): andesim tracks
which config CSRs your program actually wrote during the fast leg and
warns if any of them do not exist on the chosen cycle engine:

```
[andesim] warning: the program wrote CSRs engine vsim:<engine> does not
implement: <names> (on this engine's silicon these writes would trap; the
hybrid restore skipped them)
```

That means your program, on that engine's real silicon, would trap before
the ROI -- pick an engine that implements those CSRs, or drop the writes.
A clean run prints nothing.

### 5.8 `--kanata <file>` (+ `--objdump <file>`) -- pipeline trace of the ROI

Hybrid only (`--trigger marker|pc`). Writes a Kanata-format pipeline trace
covering exactly the measured window -- engine boot and handoff overhead
are filtered out. Open the file in
[Konata](https://github.com/shioyadan/Konata) to see the pipeline.

```sh
./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf \
  --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
  --kanata /tmp/roi.kanata
```

Add `--objdump <file>` (a text dump you generated once with
`riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump -d my.elf > my.S`) and the trace embeds the
disassembly next to each PC. `--objdump` requires `--kanata`.

Marker-mode constraint: the ELF must contain exactly one exit marker. With
more than one, the run errors out and tells you to use `--trigger pc` with
an explicit `--pc-end` instead.

### 5.9 `--gdb` (+ `--gdb-port <port>`) -- attach a debugger

Pauses the simulation at startup so a debugger can attach. Not available
in hybrid mode.

**fast** -- opens QEMU's GDB stub (default port 1234) and waits:

```sh
./andesim run --mode fast --gdb my.elf
# other terminal:
gdb-multiarch -ex 'target remote :1234' my.elf
```

**cycle** -- resets and HALTS the hart, opens the engine's JTAG bitbang
port (default 9104) in the background, then execs `$ICEMAN` -- your JTAG
debug server -- in the foreground. Point GDB at the server's own gdb port
(from your server config), not at 9104:

```sh
export ICEMAN=/path/to/jtag-debug-server
./andesim run --mode cycle --gdb --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium my.elf
```

`$ICEMAN` must speak the OpenOCD `remote_bitbang` protocol. A modern
**OpenOCD (0.12+)** works: a one-line wrapper can `exec openocd -f <cfg>`
where `<cfg>` sets `adapter driver remote_bitbang`, `remote_bitbang port
9104`, a generic `riscv` target, and a `gdb_port`. Note: the OpenOCD 0.10
bundled with Andes ICEman has a `remote_bitbang` bug against this DTM --
use a current OpenOCD.

`--gdb-port` overrides the port (fast: the QEMU stub port; cycle: the
JTAG bitbang port).

### 5.10 `-- <args...>` -- engine passthrough

Everything after a bare `--` is forwarded verbatim to the engine.
`fast`/`cycle` only: those modes run one engine process, so there is an
unambiguous target (see the VLEN example in 5.2). `hybrid` builds both
legs' command lines itself and REJECTS `--` args rather than guessing
which leg you meant -- use the dedicated flags (`--kanata`, `--objdump`,
`--mem-size`, ...) instead.

---

## 6. What a hybrid run does for you automatically

You normally do not need this section to use andesim -- it explains the
behaviors you will observe.

**Two legs, one state.** The fast leg (QEMU) runs to your ROI start, then
drains the complete architectural state -- GPRs, FPRs, vector registers,
CSRs (including the Andes-specific blocks), privilege level -- into a
state file. Program RAM is shared by construction (both legs map the same
file), so memory needs no copy. The cycle engine restores the state
through its Debug Module, runs your ROI, and drains the counters at the
exit trigger. The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta.

**Config that matters for timing rides along.** Cache-enable state (L1
`mcache_ctl`, and the L2 controller's config window on engines that have
an L2) is restored before the ROI, so a program that enabled caches during
boot measures WITH caches on -- not at the engine's reset default.

**Only what your program wrote is restored.** andesim records which config
CSRs the program actually wrote during the fast leg and restores only
those; an untouched CSR keeps the engine's own reset value, exactly like
that engine's real silicon. If the program wrote a CSR the engine does not
implement, you get the warning shown in section 5.7.

**Local memories travel too.** On engines with ILM/DLM (tightly-coupled
memories) or HVM (high-bandwidth vector memory), their content is drained
from the fast leg and loaded into the cycle engine before resume, so a
program that stages code or data there before the ROI resumes with it in
place. (A program using ILM/DLM must enable them itself via
`milmb`/`mdlmb`, as real TCM firmware does; that write is restored
automatically.) `--print-memmap` shows whether your engine has these
regions.

**First-run baseline capture.** Restoring a register over the Debug Module
costs hundreds of simulated cycles, and most state still holds reset
values. The first hybrid run of a given (engine build, ELF) pair captures
the engine's reset state once and caches it under `~/.cache/andesim/`
(honors `XDG_CACHE_HOME`); later runs skip the no-op restores, typically
cutting the vsim leg ~4x. The cache invalidates itself when the engine or
ELF changes; delete the directory to force a fresh capture. This never
changes results -- a restore is skipped only when the value is already
there.

**The ROI envelope (limits).** The measured window is assumed bare-metal,
single-hart, trap-free, interrupt-free, paging-off, and single-privilege.
S-mode CSRs (`satp`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`) are not transported. The
privilege level itself IS carried: an S/U-mode handoff also mirrors the
PMP configuration and requires an S/U-capable engine -- on an M-mode-only
engine the resume aborts with a clear pick-another-engine error. A
workload that traps, takes an interrupt, or switches privilege inside the
ROI is outside the contract. And because there is no hand-back leg,
nothing after the ROI executes.

---

## 7. Running on WSL2 and macOS

**Linux** -- native, nothing to do.

**Windows (WSL2)** -- works as Linux; two caveats:

- Keep the repo and the mmap directories on the ext4 side (`~/...`), never
  under `/mnt/c` (drvfs is slow and shared mappings are not coherent there).
- `/dev/shm` is capped by the WSL VM memory. Raise `memory=` in
  `%UserProfile%\.wslconfig` if tier 1 is too small -- or let the tier list
  fall through to `~/.cache/andesim` automatically.

`./andesim doctor` checks both (see its `mmap tiers:` section and WSL
warnings).

**macOS** -- run-only. The engines are Linux binaries, so `./andesim`
transparently re-execs the run inside a prebuilt Linux runtime image in
the podman machine VM. One-time setup:

```sh
brew install podman
podman machine init --memory 4096
podman machine start
podman pull <runtime image>      # or load a CI-built andesim-runtime:latest
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --mem-size 256M my.elf
```

Knobs: `ANDESIM_IMAGE` (image name, default `andesim-runtime:latest`),
`ANDESIM_SHM_SIZE` (container `/dev/shm`, default `3g`),
`ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE` (podman/docker). Your current directory is
bind-mounted at the same path, so relative ELF paths and output files
work. Apple Silicon runs the x86-64 image under emulation -- expect slower
wall-clock than a Linux host.

---

## 8. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Meaning / fix |
|---------|----------------|
| `multiple cycle-accurate engines; select one with --engine (have: ...)` | More than one engine is installed. Add `--engine <id>` from `list engines`. |
| `ELF is rv32 but engine '...' is rv64 -- pick a matching engine or an rv64 ELF` | Width mismatch caught up front. Rebuild the ELF for the engine's width or pick the other engine. |
| `--mode hybrid: --trigger is required` (or similar) | Hybrid always needs the ROI delimiter: `--trigger marker` (markers in source) or `--trigger pc --pc-start S --pc-end E`. |
| The run never reaches the ROI / hangs until timeout | The start trigger never fired: the binary has no markers (marker mode), or `--pc-start` is never executed. Check with `--trigger pc` on a PC you know retires, or run `./build/hotloops` to find real hot PCs. |
| `symbol '<x>' not defined in <elf>` / `malformed address '<x>'` | `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` must be a defined symbol or a valid `0x` literal. |
| `--pc-start and --pc-end resolve to the same address ... (an empty ROI measures nothing)` | Pick two distinct boundaries; equal ones would measure nothing. |
| `--mem-size ...` rejected, or `raise --mem-size or shrink the image` | Hybrid caps at `2G` minus 4 KiB (use `2047M`), and the ELF's static image must fit below the reserved V-scratch page. |
| `[hsim mmap]` chose a disk directory, or `HSIM_MMAP_DIR` run fails | `/dev/shm` was too small for the request. Either accept the disk tier, free RAM, or pin a big non-tmpfs directory via `HSIM_MMAP_DIR`. |
| `warning: the program wrote CSRs engine ... does not implement: ...` | The figure may not represent this program on this engine (on silicon those writes would trap). Choose an engine implementing those CSRs, or drop the writes. |
| `multiple ... markers in ELF -- use --mode hybrid --trigger pc ...` (with `--kanata`) | Kanata needs a unique exit; switch to `--trigger pc` and name the exit with `--pc-end`. |
| `hybrid` rejects `-- <args>` | By design: hybrid owns both legs' command lines. Use the dedicated flags instead. |
| Missing artifact / engine not discovered | Run `./andesim doctor`; it names exactly what is missing and where it looked. Setup/build is covered in `README.md`. |

---

## 9. Deeper reading

- `docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md` -- one guided exercise per trigger
  mode, with drill-down on the underlying commands.
- `docs/hotloops.md` -- the hot-loop detector's full reference.
- `docs/engine_interface.md` -- how a new simulator joins andesim (for
  engine vendors/integrators, not needed to run workloads).
- `README.md` -- what the workspace contains and how it is built.
