# andesim User Guide

Audience: an engineer who wants to RUN programs on the Andes simulators
through `./andesim` and measure cycle counts. This guide covers every
user-facing option and feature.

It assumes andesim and its engines are already installed and built
(QEMU, the vsim engines, the plugin, the runtime, and the test ELFs are
prebuilt). If something is missing, run `./andesim doctor` and hand the
report to whoever owns your install; building is covered in `README.md`,
not here.

---

## 1. What andesim is

andesim runs one RISC-V ELF on one of three models:

| Model    | What runs                              | Speed          | You get                    |
|----------|----------------------------------------|----------------|-----------------------------|
| `fast`   | QEMU only (functional)                 | MHz-class      | program output, fast        |
| `cycle`  | one cycle-accurate engine, from reset  | kHz-class      | program output + total cycles |
| `hybrid` | QEMU fast-forwards, then the cycle engine measures one region you choose | fast until your region | program output + cycles of JUST your region |

`hybrid` is the headline feature: QEMU races through boot and setup, then
hands the complete architectural state and memory to the cycle-accurate
engine (vsim, built from the real RTL), which runs only your
region-of-interest (ROI). The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta
across that window. You mark the window with a **trigger**: source-level
markers or a pair of PCs (section 5.3).

One run models ONE core. The cycle engine defines the hardware (ISA,
VLEN, caches); in hybrid mode the QEMU leg automatically inherits that
engine's ISA and VLEN so both legs execute the same architecture.

---

## 2. Check your installation

```sh
./andesim doctor          # read-only health report
./andesim list models     # the three models
./andesim list engines    # every engine you can pass to --engine
```

`doctor` checks artifacts, toolchain, runtime, engines, and the shared-memory
backing tiers, and prints WSL2 advice where relevant. A healthy install ends
with `Summary: N PASS, 0 FAIL`.

`list engines` shows what `--engine` accepts:

```
ENGINE                 TYPE  KIND            XLEN  VLEN  DLEN  ELEN
qemu64                 qemu  functional      64    -     -     -
qemu32                 qemu  functional      32    -     -     -
vsim:ax45mpv_premium   vsim  cycle-accurate  64    512   512   32
vsim:ax46mpv_advanced  vsim  cycle-accurate  64    512   512   32
```

`qemu64`/`qemu32` are the functional engines (`fast`); the `vsim:<cfg>`
entries are the cycle-accurate engines (`cycle`, and the measuring leg of
`hybrid`). `-` means the engine does not report that parameter.

Run `./andesim run -h` any time for the compact flag list; this guide is
the long version.

---

## 3. First runs

The install ships ready-made ELFs under `tests/fixtures/`; the examples
below use them. Replace with your own ELF once you have one (section 4).

### 3.1 fast -- functional, full speed

```sh
./andesim run --mode fast tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf
```

```
hello from vplat
```

Output is the program's own output, verbatim (QEMU passthrough). The exit
code of your program becomes the process exit code.

### 3.2 cycle -- one engine, from reset, total cycles

```sh
./andesim run --mode cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf
```

```
hello from vplat
[andesim] 4247 cycles
```

The engine's startup banner and verbose info log are filtered out so the
result stands alone; real warnings/errors still pass through, and the
program's exit code is propagated. The figure is the whole run from reset
-- boot, runtime init, everything.

### 3.3 hybrid -- fast-forward, then measure your region

`hybrid` needs a trigger that says where the measured window starts and
ends. The fixture below already contains ROI markers, so `--trigger
marker` works out of the box:

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
  tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf
```

```
[andesim] model=hybrid engine=vsim:ax45mpv_premium vlen=512 trigger=marker fixture=rt_c_hello
[hsim mmap] 128.0 MiB at /dev/shm (free: 251.5 GiB)
hello from QEMU1
[marker window_cycles] 54  (vsim mcycle=... - qemu mcycle=...)
PASS: --mode hybrid --trigger marker (rt_c_hello)
```

Reading the output:

- The banner names the resolved engine, its VLEN, and the trigger.
- `[hsim mmap]` names the shared-memory file backing the run (section 5.4).
- `hello from QEMU1` is the program's own output from the fast leg.
- `[marker window_cycles] 54` is the answer: your ROI took 54 cycles on
  this engine. It is the vsim `mcycle` delta across the window.
- The run ends after the ROI. Code after your ROI never executes in a
  hybrid run -- hybrid is a measuring tool, not a way to finish the program.

The first hybrid run of a given (engine, ELF) pair is a few seconds slower:
andesim captures the engine's reset state once and caches it under
`~/.cache/andesim/` so later runs can skip restoring registers that still
hold reset values (typically ~4x faster on the vsim leg). The cache
refreshes itself when the engine or the ELF changes.

---

## 4. Prepare your own program

### 4.1 Compile once, run on every engine

Link against the andesim runtime and one ELF runs on `fast`, on `cycle`,
and across a `hybrid` handoff -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting:

```sh
riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O2 \
  -B <andesim>/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
```

- Use your Andes RISC-V GCC (the one `./andesim doctor` reports).
- `-B` points gcc at the runtime artifacts; use the absolute path when
  compiling outside the repo.
- `-specs=andesim.specs` swaps in the runtime's `crt0.o`, links
  `andesim.ld` (load base `0x00100000`), and pins the library order, so no
  semihosting library can leak into the link.
- Add `v` to `-march` (e.g. `rv64gcv`) for RVV code.

For rv32 targets use the rv32 compiler and the rv32 runtime flavor:

```sh
riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O2 \
  -B <andesim>/build/runtime/rv32 -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
```

Custom build system (no gcc driver)? Link the pieces directly:

```sh
... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T build/runtime/andesim.ld \
  build/runtime/crt0.o your_prog.o -L build/runtime \
  -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
```

What the runtime gives your program, on every engine:

| Channel          | Behavior                                                       |
|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| stdio (fd 0-2)   | `printf` etc. go to the simulator console (a modeled UART)     |
| exit code        | `exit(n)` (n < 256) terminates the simulation; `n` becomes the simulator process exit code |
| file io (fd > 2) | `open`/`read`/`write` pass through to host files, resolved against the engine's working directory |

A `printf` inside a measured ROI works -- but it adds the real UART cycles
to your figure. Keep measured kernels I/O-free when you want clean numbers.

### 4.2 Mark your region (ROI markers)

For `--trigger marker`, wrap the region you want to measure:

```c
#include <andesim/ROI.h>   /* shipped with the runtime; rides the -B flag */

andesim_ROI_begin();
my_kernel(a, b, c);
andesim_ROI_end();
```

The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (architectural NOPs), so a marker
binary also runs unchanged on `fast`, on `cycle`, and on real silicon.
Ship one binary; measure when you want.

> **Measurement hygiene:** keep the kernel anchored inside the marker span
> -- read its inputs and write its outputs through memory inside the span,
> or wrap the kernel in a `__attribute__((noinline))` function called
> between the markers. The markers pin memory I/O but not register-only
> compute, so a kernel that carries live values in registers across the
> boundary may be hoisted or sunk out of the measured window by the
> compiler.

### 4.3 Cannot edit the binary? Use PC boundaries

`--trigger pc` needs no markers: you name the window with `--pc-start` and
`--pc-end`, each a symbol name or a `0x` address (section 5.3). To find
the hot region of an unknown binary first, run the bundled detector:

```sh
./build/hotloops --min-iters 10 my_kernel.elf
```

It runs the binary fast and reports the hottest loops (function, source
line, PC range) with a ready `measure:` line -- a `--pc-start`/`--pc-end`
pair you can paste straight into the hybrid command. See `docs/hotloops.md`
for the full flag reference.

---

## 5. The `run` options, one by one

Synopsis:

```
./andesim run --mode fast|cycle|hybrid [options] <ELF> [-- <engine args>]
```

### 5.1 `--mode fast|cycle|hybrid` (required)

Picks the model (section 1). Everything else keys off this choice.

### 5.2 `--engine <id>`

Picks the engine from `./andesim list engines`.

- `fast`: optional. The driver auto-selects `qemu64` or `qemu32` to match
  your ELF's width; an explicit `--engine qemu32|qemu64` overrides (with a
  warning if it disagrees with the ELF).
- `cycle` / `hybrid`: names the cycle-accurate engine. Optional only when
  exactly one is installed; with several you must choose:

  ```
  andesim run --mode cycle: model cycle: multiple cycle-accurate engines;
  select one with --engine (have: vsim:ax45mpv_premium, vsim:ax46mpv_advanced)
  ```

Width rules: `cycle`/`hybrid` reject an ELF whose width does not match the
engine, up front:

```
andesim run --mode cycle: ELF is rv32 but engine 'vsim:ax45mpv_premium' is rv64
  -- pick a matching engine or an rv64 ELF
```

Hybrid additionally requires an rv64 engine (the fast leg is rv64; an rv32
engine cannot share architectural state with it and is rejected).

VLEN: each vsim engine has a fixed VLEN (see `list engines`); in hybrid
mode the QEMU leg inherits the engine's ISA and VLEN automatically, so
both legs execute identical architecture. Supported VLEN range in hybrid:
128 to 1024 bits. A standalone `fast` run defaults to the vector-capable
`andes-ax46mpv` (rv64) / `andes-a46mpv` (rv32) CPU model; to pin an exact
VLEN there, append a `-cpu` through the passthrough tail (the last `-cpu`
wins):

```sh
./andesim run --mode fast app.elf -- -cpu andes-ax46mpv,vlen=256
```

### 5.3 `--trigger marker|pc` (+ `--pc-start`, `--pc-end`) -- hybrid only, required

The ROI delimiter for `--mode hybrid`.

**`--trigger marker`** (recommended when you can edit the source): the
window is the span strictly between `andesim_ROI_begin()` and
`andesim_ROI_end()` (section 4.2). The markers themselves are NOPs and
cost nothing.

**`--trigger pc`**: explicit boundaries, no source edits. Both flags are
required; each accepts a symbol name or a `0x` hex address:

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
  --pc-start vmatmul_kernel --pc-end 0x1002cc my.elf
```

Semantics you should know:

- The instruction at `--pc-start` executes INSIDE the measured window (the
  fast leg stops just before it; the cycle engine resumes at it -- no
  instruction is lost across the handoff). `--pc-end` is where the window
  closes.
- Symbols are resolved from the ELF's own symbol table by the driver; no
  toolchain is needed at run time. A name that is not defined fails with
  `symbol '<x>' not defined in <elf>`; a bad literal fails with
  `malformed address '<x>'`.
- Both triggers are one-shot: the first hit of the start boundary opens the
  window, the first hit of the end boundary closes it. For a function called
  many times, the window is the FIRST call.
- Start and end must resolve to different addresses; an equal pair is an
  empty window and is rejected up front:
  `--pc-start and --pc-end resolve to the same address 0x... (an empty ROI measures nothing)`.

### 5.4 `--mem-size <spec>` -- guest memory

`SPEC` accepts `256M`, `1.5G`, `2G`, or raw bytes. Per-model meaning:

| Model    | Effect |
|----------|--------|
| `hybrid` | Your program RAM (default `128M`). Max `2G` minus 4 KiB: the driver reserves one page just above your RAM for the vector-register transport, so exactly `2G` is rejected (use `2047M`) and an ELF whose static image reaches into the reserved page is rejected with `raise --mem-size or shrink the image`. |
| `fast`   | Forwarded as a plain QEMU `-m`. No 2G cap; QEMU validates the size itself. |
| `cycle`  | Ignored (the engine always models its full DRAM window); the driver says so on stderr. |

Where the hybrid shared memory lives: andesim allocates a file both legs
map. It picks the first tier with enough free space (request + 256 MiB
headroom) and always tells you which:

1. `/dev/shm` -- RAM-backed, fastest.
2. `~/.cache/andesim` -- disk-backed fallback (honors `XDG_CACHE_HOME`).

```
[hsim mmap] 2.0 GiB at /home/u/.cache/andesim (free: 2.1 TiB) (fallback: /dev/shm too small (1.2 GiB free))
```

Set `HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/path` to pin one directory with NO fallback past it
(the run fails with a hint if it cannot hold the request). Do not pin a
tmpfs mount (`/tmp` on some distros) expecting a disk ceiling -- tmpfs is
still RAM.

### 5.5 `--print-memmap` -- which addresses may a hybrid workload touch?

Prints the guest memory map for exactly the run you are about to do (same
`--engine`/`--mem-size`; the ELF is optional and only adds a fit note),
then exits without running anything. Hybrid only.

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --print-memmap --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 128M
```

```
[andesim] hybrid memory map: engine=vsim:ax45mpv_premium mem-size=128M
REGION           BASE         END          SIZE    TRANSPORT
DRAM             0x0          0x7ffffff    128M    shared mmap; content survives the handoff
V-scratch        0x8000000    0x8000fff    4K      reserved by the hybrid V transport; not program-usable
ILM              0x0          0xffff       64K     sidecar .ilm; DRAM overlay while milmb.IEN=1
DLM              0x200000     0x207fff     32K     sidecar .dlm; DRAM overlay while mdlmb.IEN=1
HVM              0x90000000   0x9003ffff   256K    sidecar .hvm
SimControl/HTIF  0xe0080000   0xe0080fff   4K      device; state does not cross the handoff
UART2            0xf0300000   0xf03fffff   1M      device (console); state does not cross the handoff
```

How to read it:

- END is the inclusive last byte.
- DRAM tracks `--mem-size`; the V-scratch page above it belongs to andesim.
- ILM/DLM/HVM rows appear only when the chosen engine has those memories
  and can transport their content; the addresses are the engine's own.
- Device state never crosses the handoff (each engine has its own UART and
  SimControl instance); only RAM content does.
- Anything NOT listed is unsupported in hybrid mode: it exists in one
  engine only, so touching it inside the ROI gives engine-specific behavior.

### 5.6 `--dry-run` -- preview without running

Valid in every mode: prints the exact engine command line(s), fully
resolved and shell-quoted, and runs nothing. `fast`/`cycle` print one
command; `hybrid` prints both legs. Use it to see precisely what a run
will execute, or to lift the command for your own scripting.

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --dry-run my.elf
# [andesim] dry-run: 2 command(s), not executed
# # command 1/2: fast-leg [qemu64]
# qemu-system-riscv64 ... -plugin .../libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=...
# # command 2/2: accurate-leg [vsim:ax45mpv_premium]
# sim_ax45mpv_premium my.elf --resume-from-qemu ... --handoff-out ...
```

### 5.7 `--verify` -- cross-check a hybrid run against a QEMU oracle

A hybrid run normally proves only that a cycle figure came out. `--verify`
(hybrid only, default off) re-runs the same ELF on pure QEMU up to the ROI
exit and compares the architectural state field by field against what the
cycle engine drained:

```
[marker window_cycles] 46  (vsim mcycle=... - qemu mcycle=...)
[state-diff] PASS: 109 fields match (counters and passthrough CSRs excluded)
[verify] PASS: vsim drain matches the QEMU oracle
```

A mismatch lists each differing field and exits non-zero:

```
[state-diff] x10: ref=0x3d got=0x0
[state-diff] FAIL: 1 mismatch(es) (115 fields compared)
```

What is compared: the PC, all GPRs, FPRs (when FP state is live), the
vector registers and V CSRs (when V is live), the privilege level, and the
M-mode CSRs that round-trip through the handoff. Deliberately excluded:
`mcycle`/`minstret` (the engines count differently by design), `mip`
(hardware-driven pending bits), and a few CSRs whose reset values
legitimately differ between engines.

Two costs: one extra QEMU run of the whole program (cheap), and a full
register read-back over the Debug Module at the ROI exit (not cheap --
without `--verify` the exit drain reads only the two counters). Expect a
`--verify` run to take noticeably longer; the cycle figure itself is not
affected.

Related, printed on EVERY hybrid run (not just `--verify`): andesim tracks
which config CSRs your program actually wrote during the fast leg and
warns if any of them do not exist on the chosen cycle engine:

```
[andesim] warning: the program wrote CSRs engine vsim:<engine> does not
implement: <names> (on this engine's silicon these writes would trap; the
hybrid restore skipped them)
```

That means your program, on that engine's real silicon, would trap before
the ROI -- pick an engine that implements those CSRs, or drop the writes.
A clean run prints nothing.

### 5.8 `--kanata <file>` (+ `--objdump <file>`) -- pipeline trace of the ROI

Hybrid only (`--trigger marker|pc`). Writes a Kanata-format pipeline trace
covering exactly the measured window -- engine boot and handoff overhead
are filtered out. Open the file in
[Konata](https://github.com/shioyadan/Konata) to see the pipeline.

```sh
./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf \
  --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
  --kanata /tmp/roi.kanata
```

Add `--objdump <file>` (a text dump you generated once with
`riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump -d my.elf > my.S`) and the trace embeds the
disassembly next to each PC. `--objdump` requires `--kanata`.

Marker-mode constraint: the ELF must contain exactly one exit marker. With
more than one, the run errors out and tells you to use `--trigger pc` with
an explicit `--pc-end` instead.

### 5.9 `--gdb` (+ `--gdb-port <port>`) -- attach a debugger

Pauses the simulation at startup so a debugger can attach. Not available
in hybrid mode.

**fast** -- opens QEMU's GDB stub (default port 1234) and waits:

```sh
./andesim run --mode fast --gdb my.elf
# other terminal:
gdb-multiarch -ex 'target remote :1234' my.elf
```

**cycle** -- resets and HALTS the hart, opens the engine's JTAG bitbang
port (default 9104) in the background, then execs `$ICEMAN` -- your JTAG
debug server -- in the foreground. Point GDB at the server's own gdb port
(from your server config), not at 9104:

```sh
export ICEMAN=/path/to/jtag-debug-server
./andesim run --mode cycle --gdb --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium my.elf
```

`$ICEMAN` must speak the OpenOCD `remote_bitbang` protocol. A modern
**OpenOCD (0.12+)** works: a one-line wrapper can `exec openocd -f <cfg>`
where `<cfg>` sets `adapter driver remote_bitbang`, `remote_bitbang port
9104`, a generic `riscv` target, and a `gdb_port`. Note: the OpenOCD 0.10
bundled with Andes ICEman has a `remote_bitbang` bug against this DTM --
use a current OpenOCD.

`--gdb-port` overrides the port (fast: the QEMU stub port; cycle: the
JTAG bitbang port).

### 5.10 `-- <args...>` -- engine passthrough

Everything after a bare `--` is forwarded verbatim to the engine.
`fast`/`cycle` only: those modes run one engine process, so there is an
unambiguous target (see the VLEN example in 5.2). `hybrid` builds both
legs' command lines itself and REJECTS `--` args rather than guessing
which leg you meant -- use the dedicated flags (`--kanata`, `--objdump`,
`--mem-size`, ...) instead.

---

## 6. What a hybrid run does for you automatically

You normally do not need this section to use andesim -- it explains the
behaviors you will observe.

**Two legs, one state.** The fast leg (QEMU) runs to your ROI start, then
drains the complete architectural state -- GPRs, FPRs, vector registers,
CSRs (including the Andes-specific blocks), privilege level -- into a
state file. Program RAM is shared by construction (both legs map the same
file), so memory needs no copy. The cycle engine restores the state
through its Debug Module, runs your ROI, and drains the counters at the
exit trigger. The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta.

**Config that matters for timing rides along.** Cache-enable state (L1
`mcache_ctl`, and the L2 controller's config window on engines that have
an L2) is restored before the ROI, so a program that enabled caches during
boot measures WITH caches on -- not at the engine's reset default.

**Only what your program wrote is restored.** andesim records which config
CSRs the program actually wrote during the fast leg and restores only
those; an untouched CSR keeps the engine's own reset value, exactly like
that engine's real silicon. If the program wrote a CSR the engine does not
implement, you get the warning shown in section 5.7.

**Local memories travel too.** On engines with ILM/DLM (tightly-coupled
memories) or HVM (high-bandwidth vector memory), their content is drained
from the fast leg and loaded into the cycle engine before resume, so a
program that stages code or data there before the ROI resumes with it in
place. (A program using ILM/DLM must enable them itself via
`milmb`/`mdlmb`, as real TCM firmware does; that write is restored
automatically.) `--print-memmap` shows whether your engine has these
regions.

**First-run baseline capture.** Restoring a register over the Debug Module
costs hundreds of simulated cycles, and most state still holds reset
values. The first hybrid run of a given (engine build, ELF) pair captures
the engine's reset state once and caches it under `~/.cache/andesim/`
(honors `XDG_CACHE_HOME`); later runs skip the no-op restores, typically
cutting the vsim leg ~4x. The cache invalidates itself when the engine or
ELF changes; delete the directory to force a fresh capture. This never
changes results -- a restore is skipped only when the value is already
there.

**The ROI envelope (limits).** The measured window is assumed bare-metal,
single-hart, trap-free, interrupt-free, paging-off, and single-privilege.
S-mode CSRs (`satp`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`) are not transported. The
privilege level itself IS carried: an S/U-mode handoff also mirrors the
PMP configuration and requires an S/U-capable engine -- on an M-mode-only
engine the resume aborts with a clear pick-another-engine error. A
workload that traps, takes an interrupt, or switches privilege inside the
ROI is outside the contract. And because there is no hand-back leg,
nothing after the ROI executes.

---

## 7. Running on WSL2 and macOS

**Linux** -- native, nothing to do.

**Windows (WSL2)** -- works as Linux; two caveats:

- Keep the repo and the mmap directories on the ext4 side (`~/...`), never
  under `/mnt/c` (drvfs is slow and shared mappings are not coherent there).
- `/dev/shm` is capped by the WSL VM memory. Raise `memory=` in
  `%UserProfile%\.wslconfig` if tier 1 is too small -- or let the tier list
  fall through to `~/.cache/andesim` automatically.

`./andesim doctor` checks both (see its `mmap tiers:` section and WSL
warnings).

**macOS** -- run-only. The engines are Linux binaries, so `./andesim`
transparently re-execs the run inside a prebuilt Linux runtime image in
the podman machine VM. One-time setup:

```sh
brew install podman
podman machine init --memory 4096
podman machine start
podman pull <runtime image>      # or load a CI-built andesim-runtime:latest
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --mem-size 256M my.elf
```

Knobs: `ANDESIM_IMAGE` (image name, default `andesim-runtime:latest`),

---

## 8. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Meaning / fix |
|---------|----------------|
| `multiple cycle-accurate engines; select one with --engine (have: ...)` | More than one engine is installed. Add `--engine <id>` from `list engines`. |
| `ELF is rv32 but engine '...' is rv64 -- pick a matching engine or an rv64 ELF` | Width mismatch caught up front. Rebuild the ELF for the engine's width or pick the other engine. |
| `--mode hybrid: --trigger is required` (or similar) | Hybrid always needs the ROI delimiter: `--trigger marker` (markers in source) or `--trigger pc --pc-start S --pc-end E`. |
| The run never reaches the ROI / hangs until timeout | The start trigger never fired: the binary has no markers (marker mode), or `--pc-start` is never executed. Check with `--trigger pc` on a PC you know retires, or run `./build/hotloops` to find real hot PCs. |
| `symbol '<x>' not defined in <elf>` / `malformed address '<x>'` | `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` must be a defined symbol or a valid `0x` literal. |
| `--pc-start and --pc-end resolve to the same address ... (an empty ROI measures nothing)` | Pick two distinct boundaries; equal ones would measure nothing. |
| `--mem-size ...` rejected, or `raise --mem-size or shrink the image` | Hybrid caps at `2G` minus 4 KiB (use `2047M`), and the ELF's static image must fit below the reserved V-scratch page. |
| `[hsim mmap]` chose a disk directory, or `HSIM_MMAP_DIR` run fails | `/dev/shm` was too small for the request. Either accept the disk tier, free RAM, or pin a big non-tmpfs directory via `HSIM_MMAP_DIR`. |
| `warning: the program wrote CSRs engine ... does not implement: ...` | The figure may not represent this program on this engine (on silicon those writes would trap). Choose an engine implementing those CSRs, or drop the writes. |
| `multiple ... markers in ELF -- use --mode hybrid --trigger pc ...` (with `--kanata`) | Kanata needs a unique exit; switch to `--trigger pc` and name the exit with `--pc-end`. |
| `hybrid` rejects `-- <args>` | By design: hybrid owns both legs' command lines. Use the dedicated flags instead. |
| Missing artifact / engine not discovered | Run `./andesim doctor`; it names exactly what is missing and where it looked. Setup/build is covered in `README.md`. |

+## 6. What a hybrid run does for you automatically
-The runtime ships prebuilt as `libandesim_runtime.a`. Build it once
-(`scripts/build_all.sh runtime`, or any fixture build does it implicitly),
-then compile with two extra flags (same line for every engine; no `-mvh`,
-no `-lgloss_vh`):
+You normally do not need this section to use andesim -- it explains the
+behaviors you will observe.
-"$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
-  -B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
+**Two legs, one state.** The fast leg (QEMU) runs to your ROI start, then
+drains the complete architectural state -- GPRs, FPRs, vector registers,
+CSRs (including the Andes-specific blocks), privilege level -- into a
+state file. Program RAM is shared by construction (both legs map the same
+file), so memory needs no copy. The cycle engine restores the state
+through its Debug Module, runs your ROI, and drains the counters at the
+exit trigger. The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta.
-`-B` points gcc at the built artifacts (use the absolute path to
-`<repo>/build/runtime` when compiling outside the repo);
-`-specs=andesim.specs` swaps the startfile to the runtime's `crt0.o`,
-adds `-T andesim.ld` (load base `0x00100000`), and rewrites the library
-list to `--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc --end-group`, so no
-libgloss or semihosting can leak into the link.
+**Config that matters for timing rides along.** Cache-enable state (L1
+`mcache_ctl`, and the L2 controller's config window on engines that have
+an L2) is restored before the ROI, so a program that enabled caches during
+boot measures WITH caches on -- not at the engine's reset default.
-Without the gcc driver (a custom build system), link the pieces directly:
+**Only what your program wrote is restored.** andesim records which config
+CSRs the program actually wrote during the fast leg and restores only
+those; an untouched CSR keeps the engine's own reset value, exactly like
+that engine's real silicon. If the program wrote a CSR the engine does not
+implement, you get the warning shown in section 5.7.
-... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T build/runtime/andesim.ld \
-  build/runtime/crt0.o your_prog.o -L build/runtime \
-  -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
+**Local memories travel too.** On engines with ILM/DLM (tightly-coupled
+memories) or HVM (high-bandwidth vector memory), their content is drained
+from the fast leg and loaded into the cycle engine before resume, so a
+program that stages code or data there before the ROI resumes with it in
+place. (A program using ILM/DLM must enable them itself via
+`milmb`/`mdlmb`, as real TCM firmware does; that write is restored
+automatically.) `--print-memmap` shows whether your engine has these
+regions.
-Sources live in `runtime/` (crt0.S boot, trap.S + handler.c trap
-diagnostics, vplat_syscalls.c newlib stubs). `crt0.o` is shipped next to
-the archive, not inside it: nothing references `_start`, so the linker
-would never extract it from a `.a`.
+**First-run baseline capture.** Restoring a register over the Debug Module
+costs hundreds of simulated cycles, and most state still holds reset
+values. The first hybrid run of a given (engine build, ELF) pair captures
+the engine's reset state once and caches it under `~/.cache/andesim/`
+(honors `XDG_CACHE_HOME`); later runs skip the no-op restores, typically
+cutting the vsim leg ~4x. The cache invalidates itself when the engine or
+ELF changes; delete the directory to force a fresh capture. This never
+changes results -- a restore is skipped only when the value is already
+there.
+**The ROI envelope (limits).** The measured window is assumed bare-metal,
+single-hart, trap-free, interrupt-free, paging-off, and single-privilege.
+S-mode CSRs (`satp`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`) are not transported. The
+privilege level itself IS carried: an S/U-mode handoff also mirrors the
+PMP configuration and requires an S/U-capable engine -- on an M-mode-only
+engine the resume aborts with a clear pick-another-engine error. A
+workload that traps, takes an interrupt, or switches privilege inside the
+ROI is outside the contract. And because there is no hand-back leg,
+nothing after the ROI executes.
-The runtime builds for **both** widths from two toolchains (`HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN`
-= rv64, `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32` = rv32; section 1.3). `scripts/build_all.sh
-runtime` builds both when `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32` is set:
-- rv64 -> `build/runtime/` (link `-B build/runtime`, as above).
-- rv32 -> `build/runtime/rv32/` (link `-B build/runtime/rv32`).
+## 7. Running on WSL2 and macOS
-The rv32 link is the same shape with the rv32 compiler and `-march=rv32gc
--mabi=ilp32d`:
+**Linux** -- native, nothing to do.
-"$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc" -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 \

+  under `/mnt/c` (drvfs is slow and shared mappings are not coherent there).

-  with a warning if it disagrees with the ELF).

-  engine, up front, instead of a cryptic failure deep inside the engine:
+`./andesim doctor` checks both (see its `mmap tiers:` section and WSL
+warnings).

-  andesim run --mode cycle: ELF is rv32 but engine 'vsim:ax45mpv_premium' is rv64
-    -- pick a matching engine or an rv64 ELF

+transparently re-execs the run inside a prebuilt Linux runtime image in
+the podman machine VM. One-time setup:
-Ready-made fixtures: `vplat_hello.elf` (stdio + exit), `vplat_exit41.elf`

-  simulation and becomes the simulator process exit code on both engines
-- **File io** is host-passthrough: paths resolve relative to the engine

-  byte-for-byte (newlib->Linux `O_*` translation, `st_mode`/`st_size`-only
-  stat writeback).

-  (`slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1` -- rd=x0 discards the result), so they execute
-  as NOPs on every engine and on silicon: one marker ELF runs standalone on

-| `QEMU 1 expected exit 200, got 0`                      | Trigger never fired. Wrong mode / wrong PC.     |
-| `QEMU 1 expected exit 200, got 124`                    | `timeout` killed the plugin. Increase `TIMEOUT` or tune the target.  |

-| Whole suite times out under `scripts/run_e2e.sh`               | Set `JOBS=8`. Default 128 saturates a 128-core host.                 |

+| `--pc-start and --pc-end resolve to the same address ... (an empty ROI measures nothing)` | Pick two distinct boundaries; equal ones would measure nothing. |
+| `--mem-size ...` rejected, or `raise --mem-size or shrink the image` | Hybrid caps at `2G` minus 4 KiB (use `2047M`), and the ELF's static image must fit below the reserved V-scratch page. |

content.text:
Rewrote `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` as a pure end-user guide: 615 lines (down from ~1240), zero build content, organized around using the options and features.

**Structure:**
1. **What andesim is** - the 3-model mental model, hybrid explained in one paragraph
2. **Check your installation** - `doctor`, `list models`, `list engines`
3. **First runs** - one real fast/cycle/hybrid run each, with the actual output explained line by line (including the first-run baseline-cache slowness)
4. **Prepare your own program** - the two-flag compile line (rv64 + rv32), what the runtime gives you (stdio/exit/file io), ROI markers with the measurement-hygiene note, and hotloops for binaries you can't edit
5. **The `run` options, one by one** - a subsection per flag: `--mode`, `--engine` (width rules, VLEN), `--trigger`/`--pc-start`/`--pc-end` (boundary semantics, one-shot), `--mem-size` (per-mode table, tiers, `HSIM_MMAP_DIR`), `--print-memmap`, `--dry-run`, `--verify` (plus the wrote-unimplemented-CSRs warning), `--kanata`/`--objdump`, `--gdb`/`--gdb-port`, and `--` passthrough
6. **What a hybrid run does automatically** - state/RAM/LM/HVM transport, write-mask restore, baseline cache, and the ROI envelope (limits)
7. **WSL2 and macOS** notes
8. **Troubleshooting** - symptom-to-fix table using the real error strings
9. **Deeper reading** - four pointers, with build/setup delegated to `README.md`

**Grounding:** every sample output comes from a run I executed just now (doctor, cycle `4247 cycles`, the 5-line hybrid output, the memmap table), and every quoted error message was checked against the driver source (`multiple cycle-accurate engines...`, `symbol '<x>' not defined...`, `--trigger marker\|pc is required...`, the empty-ROI rejection, `raise --mem-size or shrink the image`).

**Dropped as requested:** cloning, `config.env`, toolchain setup, `setup.sh`/`build_all.sh`, fixture building, plugin args, vsim CLI flags, the underlying two-leg invocations, and the test-suite sections - all developer surface, still covered by `README.md`/`CLAUDE.md`.

# ROADMAP: full Andes-V5 CSR transport coverage

**Goal.** For the supported envelope - bare-metal, single-hart, **M-mode or
M+U-mode**, trap-free ROI - verify the hybrid handoff correctly exchanges state
for **every** CSR in `AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7`, with a per-section test and a
machine-checked guarantee that nothing is missed.

**Predecessor.** `docs/andes_csr_transport_ROADMAP.md` (RESOLVED) added the v3
Andes block - 13 scalar CSRs + PMA - and the capability-gating flywheel. This
ROADMAP reuses that exact pattern (one X-macro list, capability-gated, parity
flywheel) to cover the remaining writable M-mode CSRs across the whole spec.

## The reality (why not "all 232 round-trip")

The spec's Chapter 5 yields **232 CSR rows**. They split three ways (full table:
`docs/csr_coverage.ipynb`, data: `tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv`):

| group | count | what we do |
|-------|-------|------------|
| **carried today** | 41 | already round-trip through `hybrid_state_v1` |
| **ADD** | 49 | writable M-mode plain state -> expand transport (this ROADMAP) |
| **correctly excluded** | 142 | read-only config (29), RV32 shadows (21), side-effecting (11), N-ext (8), indirect-access (7), debug-internal (6), S/H mode-unsupported (57), other (3) |

"Exchange state" only has meaning for **writable plain architectural state**. A
read-only config register (`mvendorid`, `mmsc_cfg`) has nothing to exchange - each
engine derives it. A side-effecting CSR (`pushmcause` pushes to the stack,
`mcctlcommand` issues a cache op) is an instruction in CSR clothing, not state.
Those are excluded **with a documented reason**, asserted by the guard - that is
how "nothing missed" is satisfied without 142 meaningless round-trips.

## Architecture

Three pillars, each reusing a pattern already proven in the repo:

1. **One X-macro list = one source of truth.** New writable M-mode CSRs go in a
   single `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST(X)` in `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`, exactly like
   the existing `HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST`. Every consumer (QEMU plugin drain,
   `ResumeDriver` restore, `StateDrain` re-read, driver `state_diff` verify)
   iterates the list, so **adding a CSR is one line** and no consumer drifts.

2. **Capability-gated, not assumed.** Each new CSR maps to a feature gate in
   `andes_caps.hpp` (`andes_gate_for`). An engine reports the CSRs it actually
   implements via `--describe`; the driver skips `--verify` on the rest. Premium
   (M-only) implements a subset; the gate prevents a hang on an absent CSR. This
   is the existing capability flywheel, extended.

3. **A completeness guard = the flywheel.** `tests/andes_csr/` holds the spec
   inventory snapshot + the coverage matrix. The guard test cross-checks
   inventory <-> matrix <-> `state_abi.h` and **fails CI** on any drift: a CSR the
   spec adds, a CSR transported that the matrix marks excluded, or a promised CSR
   missing from the ABI. Refresh path: `scripts/extract_csr_inventory.py`
   (PDF -> inventory) then `scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py` (inventory -> matrix).

## Per-feature definition of done

Each expansion feature (F3+) is ONE CSR block and must deliver all of:

- [ ] `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST` X() line(s) in the ABI submodule (+ pin bump in andesim and vsim)
- [ ] QEMU plugin drains it (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`)
- [ ] `ResumeDriver` restores it (tolerant, capability-gated)
- [ ] `StateDrain` re-reads it
- [ ] `state_diff` verifies it (with the right exclusions, e.g. HW-driven latches)
- [ ] `andes_caps.hpp` gate entry + `classify_csr_coverage.py` stays in parity
- [ ] one per-section round-trip fixture under `tests/fixtures/`, run on premium
- [ ] guard test still green; ROADMAP state updated

Cross-repo note: the ABI lives in the `andesim_abi` submodule, pinned by BOTH
andesim and the external vsim. A block touches 3 repos (ABI + vsim consumers +
qemu_plugin), like the v3 Andes block did.

## Features

| ID | Feature | CSRs | State |
|----|---------|------|-------|
| F1 | Completeness guard test | (foundation) | **DONE** (`e0a6891`) |
| F2 | ABI v4 `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST` (51 CSRs) + all consumers + capability gates | (structural) | **DONE** (ABI `1e07582`, vsim `9d972ba`, andesim `8b952d6`) |
| F5 | Counters / perf-monitor | mcountinhibit, mhpmevent3-6, mcounterinten (+ HW counters restored, verify-excluded) | **DONE** (`fcf5ecb`/`e321da1`) - found + fixed the mcounterwen UMODE gate bug |
| F6 | Andes trap-save (mdcause subset) | mdcause | **DONE** (`b110977`) - transported; verify-excluded (vsim HW-set) |
| F11 | Triggers | tselect, tdata2, mcontext (round-trip); tdata1/tcontrol verify-excluded | **DONE** (`b110977`) |
| F3 | Machine Configuration | menvcfg, mseccfg | FORWARD-LOOKING (premium gates UMODE/EPMP off; no engine to verify) |
| F4 | NMI handling | mnscratch, mnepc, mncause, mnstatus, mnvec, mrnxvec | FORWARD-LOOKING (SMRNMI off) |
| F7 | CLIC | mtvt, mintthresh, mcirq_entry | FORWARD-LOOKING (CLIC off) |
| F8 | State-enable | mstateen0-3 | FORWARD-LOOKING (SMSTATEEN off) |
| F9 | Memory / peripheral | mppib, mfiob, mcctlbeginaddr, mcctldata | FORWARD-LOOKING (PPI/FIO/CCTL off) |
| F10 | PMA extend (16 -> 48) | pmacfg4/6/8/10, pmaaddr16-47 | DEFERRED (premium has 4 PMA entries; user chose premium-only) |
| F12 | U-delta | uzobctl, umisc_ctl, sleepvalue, ucctlbeginaddr | FORWARD-LOOKING (UMODE off; needs M+U engine) |
| F13 | Docs + verification-status (this section) | (the 142 excluded) | **DONE** |

## Outcome (2026-06-28)

All 51 writable M-mode CSRs are transported in ABI v4, capability-gated. On the
verification engine (ax45mpv_premium, M-only) **25** are implemented and gated on;
the other **26** are gated off and ride forward-looking for an engine that
implements the feature (CLIC, Smrnmi, Smstateen, ePMP, U-mode, ...).

Of the 25 premium-gated CSRs, verification status:
- **round-trip tested** (in-ROI self-check, marker + pc): mcountinhibit,
  mhpmevent3/4 (and 5/6 by the same gate), mcounterinten, tselect, tdata2,
  mcontext (`tests/fixtures/rt_m_ext_counters.S`, `rt_m_ext_trigcause.S`).
- **transported + restored, verify-excluded** (engine-divergent, like
  msp_bound/mip): mhpmcounter3-6 (HW counters), mdcause (vsim HW-set),
  tdata1/tcontrol (trigger defaults), mcontext at arbitrary width.

"Nothing missed" is enforced not by a fixture per CSR but by the machine-checked
guard (`tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py`): every one of the 232 spec CSRs is
classified, the matrix matches the offline policy, and the ABI transports exactly
the matrix-approved set. The forward-looking sections (F3/F4/F7/F8/F9/F12) are
verified-correct *as transported-and-gated-off* by the guard + the parity
flywheel; their round-trip verification waits on a capable engine.

## Risks / judgment calls already baked in

- **Side-effecting CSRs stay excluded even under "expand all"**: `pushmcause`,
  `pushmepc`, `pushmxstatus`, `mnxti`, `mscratchcsw`, `mscratchcswl`,
  `mcctlcommand`, `mintsel_jal` - reading/writing performs an action, so the value
  is not state. Documented per-CSR in the matrix.
- **Triggers (F11) touch the Debug Module** the handoff itself drives. Transported
  last, behind its own gate, with a fixture that checks the DM handshake still
  works.
- **Premium is M-only**: F12 (U-delta) ships in the ABI but cannot be round-trip
  tested until an M+U engine run (d23). Marked deferred, not skipped.

| F10 | PMA extend (16 -> 48) | pmacfg4/6/8/10, pmaaddr16-47 | DEFERRED (premium has 4 PMA entries; user chose premium-only) |
| F12 | U-delta | uzobctl, umisc_ctl, sleepvalue, ucctlbeginaddr | FORWARD-LOOKING (UMODE off; needs M+U engine) |
| F13 | Docs + verification-status (this section) | (the 142 excluded) | **DONE** |

## Outcome (2026-06-28)

All 51 writable M-mode CSRs are transported in ABI v4, capability-gated. On the
verification engine (ax45mpv_premium, M-only) **25** are implemented and gated on;
the other **26** are gated off and ride forward-looking for an engine that
implements the feature (CLIC, Smrnmi, Smstateen, ePMP, U-mode, ...).

Of the 25 premium-gated CSRs, verification status:
- **round-trip tested** (in-ROI self-check, marker + pc): mcountinhibit,
  mhpmevent3/4 (and 5/6 by the same gate), mcounterinten, tselect, tdata2,
  mcontext (`tests/fixtures/rt_m_ext_counters.S`, `rt_m_ext_trigcause.S`).
- **transported + restored, verify-excluded** (engine-divergent, like
  msp_bound/mip): mhpmcounter3-6 (HW counters), mdcause (vsim HW-set),
  tdata1/tcontrol (trigger defaults), mcontext at arbitrary width.

"Nothing missed" is enforced not by a fixture per CSR but by the machine-checked
guard (`tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py`): every one of the 232 spec CSRs is
classified, the matrix matches the offline policy, and the ABI transports exactly
the matrix-approved set. The forward-looking sections (F3/F4/F7/F8/F9/F12) are
verified-correct *as transported-and-gated-off* by the guard + the parity
flywheel; their round-trip verification waits on a capable engine.

## Risks / judgment calls already baked in

- **Side-effecting CSRs stay excluded even under "expand all"**: `pushmcause`,
  `pushmepc`, `pushmxstatus`, `mnxti`, `mscratchcsw`, `mscratchcswl`,
  `mcctlcommand`, `mintsel_jal` - reading/writing performs an action, so the value
  is not state. Documented per-CSR in the matrix.
- **Triggers (F11) touch the Debug Module** the handoff itself drives. Transported
  last, behind its own gate, with a fixture that checks the DM handshake still
  works.
- **Premium is M-only**: F12 (U-delta) ships in the ABI but cannot be round-trip
  tested until an M+U engine run (d23). Marked deferred, not skipped.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Classify every spec CSR by its hybrid-handoff transport disposition.

The OFFLINE mirror of the wire-format transport set. It reads the spec inventory
snapshot (tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv, produced by extract_csr_inventory.py)
and assigns each CSR a disposition under the supported envelope: bare-metal,
single-hart, M-mode or M+U-mode, trap-free ROI.

The policy here must match what include/hybrid/state_abi.h actually transports.
The guard test (tests/andes_csr/test_csr_coverage_complete.*) cross-checks the
two, so a CSR added to the ABI without a matching disposition (or vice versa)
fails CI -- the "nothing missed" flywheel.

Dispositions (see docs/csr_coverage.ipynb for the full legend):
  TRANSPORT_NOW  already carried in hybrid_state_v1
  NEW            writable M-mode plain state -- expansion target
  NEW_TRIG       debug-trigger CSR (shares the Debug Module; transported guarded)
  NEW_UDELTA     U-mode Andes control; transported, exercised only in M+U
  CONST_RO       read-only config/info -- engine derives it; nothing to exchange
  EXCL_RV32      RV32 high-half shadow -- irrelevant on RV64
  EXCL_SIDEFX    read/write has side effects -- not architectural state
  EXCL_W1C_HW    write-1-clear, hardware-driven (like mip)
  EXCL_INDIRECT  miselect/mireg access mechanism, not a direct register
  EXCL_NEXT      U-mode N-extension trap state (trap-free ROI + usually absent)
  EXCL_DEBUG     Debug-mode CSR the handoff itself drives
  EXCL_MODE      S-mode / Hypervisor -- outside the M / M+U envelope
  EXCL_TRAP      detailed trap-cause latch, live only after a trap

Usage:
  classify_csr_coverage.py <csr_inventory.csv>            # write csr_coverage.csv beside it
  classify_csr_coverage.py <csr_inventory.csv> --stdout   # print, do not write
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import sys
from pathlib import Path

# CSRs already carried in hybrid_state_v1 today (Bucket A). Names as the spec
# summary tables print them (range rows kept verbatim, e.g. pmpaddr1~63).
TRANSPORT_NOW = {
    "mstatus", "mepc", "mtvec", "mcause", "mtval", "mscratch", "medeleg",
    "mideleg", "mie", "mip", "mcycle", "minstret", "satp", "fcsr", "frm",
    "fﬂags",  # "fflags" with the fi-ligature the PDF emits
    "JVT", "mcache_ctl", "mmisc_ctl", "mxstatus", "mpft_ctl", "mclk_ctl",
    "milmb", "mdlmb", "mecc_code", "mhsp_ctl", "msp_bound", "msp_base",
    "mcountermask_m", "uitb", "ucode",
    "pmpcfg0", "pmpcfg1", "pmpcfg2", "pmpcfg3", "pmpcfg4~15",
    "pmpaddr0", "pmpaddr1~63",
    "pmacfg0", "pmacfg2", "pmaaddr0~47",
}

# Per-name decisions that override the structural defaults below.
OVERRIDE = {
    "misa": "CONST_RO", "tinfo": "CONST_RO", "tdata3": "CONST_RO",
    "mintstatus": "EXCL_RO",
    # side-effecting: reading or writing performs an action, so the value is not
    # state to round-trip.
    "mnxti": "EXCL_SIDEFX", "mscratchcsw": "EXCL_SIDEFX",
    "mscratchcswl": "EXCL_SIDEFX", "mcctlcommand": "EXCL_SIDEFX",
    "mintsel_jal": "EXCL_SIDEFX", "pushmcause": "EXCL_SIDEFX",
    "pushmepc": "EXCL_SIDEFX", "pushmxstatus": "EXCL_SIDEFX",
    "wfe": "EXCL_SIDEFX", "txevt": "EXCL_SIDEFX", "ucctlcommand": "EXCL_SIDEFX",
    "mcounterovf": "EXCL_W1C_HW",
    "miselect": "EXCL_INDIRECT", "mireg": "EXCL_INDIRECT",
    "mireg2": "EXCL_INDIRECT", "mireg3": "EXCL_INDIRECT",
    "mireg4": "EXCL_INDIRECT", "mireg5": "EXCL_INDIRECT",
    "mireg6": "EXCL_INDIRECT",
    "dcsr": "EXCL_DEBUG", "dpc": "EXCL_DEBUG", "dscratch0": "EXCL_DEBUG",
    "dscratch1": "EXCL_DEBUG", "scontext": "EXCL_MODE",
    # writable M-mode plain state to add (the expansion).
    "menvcfg": "NEW", "mseccfg": "NEW", "mnscratch": "NEW", "mnepc": "NEW",
    "mncause": "NEW", "mnstatus": "NEW", "mnvec": "NEW", "mrnxvec": "NEW",
    "mtvt": "NEW", "mintthresh": "NEW", "mcounteren": "NEW",
    "mcountinhibit": "NEW", "mhpmcounter3~6": "NEW", "mhpmevent3~6": "NEW",
    "mcounterwen": "NEW", "mcounterinten": "NEW", "mcountermask_s": "NEW",
    "mcountermask_u": "NEW", "mdcause": "NEW", "mslideleg": "NEW",
    "msavestatus": "NEW", "msaveepc1": "NEW", "msavecause1": "NEW",
    "msaveepc2": "NEW", "msavecause2": "NEW", "msavedcause1": "NEW",
    "msavedcause2": "NEW", "mstateen0": "NEW", "mstateen1": "NEW",
    "mstateen2": "NEW", "mstateen3": "NEW", "mppib": "NEW", "mfiob": "NEW",
    "mﬁob": "NEW",  # fi-ligature variant the PDF emits
    "mcctlbeginaddr": "NEW", "mcctldata": "NEW", "mirq_entry": "NEW",
    "pmacfg4": "NEW", "pmacfg6": "NEW", "pmacfg8": "NEW", "pmacfg10": "NEW",
    "tselect": "NEW_TRIG", "mcontrol/tdata1": "NEW_TRIG", "tdata2": "NEW_TRIG",
    "tcontrol": "NEW_TRIG", "mcontext": "NEW_TRIG",
    "uzobctl": "NEW_UDELTA", "umisc_ctl": "NEW_UDELTA",
    "sleepvalue": "NEW_UDELTA", "ucctlbeginaddr": "NEW_UDELTA",
    "udcause": "EXCL_TRAP",
}

RV32_ONLY = {
    "mcycleh", "minstreth", "mhpmcounter3h~6h", "mhpmevent3h~6h", "menvcfgh",
    "mseccfgh", "mstateen0h", "mstateen1h", "mstateen2h", "mstateen3h",
    "mcache_ctl2", "cycleh", "timeh", "instreth", "hpmcounter3h~6h",
    "pmacfg1", "pmacfg3", "pmacfg5", "pmacfg7", "pmacfg9", "pmacfg11",
}


def classify(addr, priv, name, mode, section):
    if name in TRANSPORT_NOW:
        return "TRANSPORT_NOW"
    if name in OVERRIDE:
        return OVERRIDE[name]
    if name in RV32_ONLY:
        return "EXCL_RV32"
    if mode in ("S-std", "S-andes", "H-std"):
        return "EXCL_MODE"
    if mode == "D-std" or name in ("dexc2dbg", "ddcause"):
        return "EXCL_DEBUG"
    if priv in ("MRO", "SRO", "URO", "DRO", "HRO"):
        return "CONST_RO"
    if mode == "U-std" and section == "N Extension CSRs":
        return "EXCL_NEXT"
    if mode == "U-std" and section == "Counter/Timer Registers":
        return "CONST_RO"
    raise SystemExit(f"unclassified CSR: {addr} {name} ({mode}/{section})")


def main(argv):
    if not argv:
        print(__doc__)
        return 2
    inv = Path(argv[0])
    to_stdout = "--stdout" in argv[1:]
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(inv.open()))
    out = [[r["addr"], r["priv"], r["name"], r["mode"], r["section"],
            classify(r["addr"], r["priv"], r["name"], r["mode"], r["section"])]
           for r in rows]
    if to_stdout:
        w = csv.writer(sys.stdout)
    else:
        dst = inv.with_name("csr_coverage.csv").open("w", newline="")
        w = csv.writer(dst)
    w.writerow(["addr", "priv", "name", "mode", "section", "decision"])
    w.writerows(out)
    if not to_stdout:
        print(f"wrote {inv.with_name('csr_coverage.csv')} ({len(out)} rows)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CSR coverage completeness guard (the "nothing missed" flywheel).
#
# Fails if the spec inventory snapshot, the coverage matrix, and the wire format
# (include/hybrid/state_abi.h) ever drift apart -- a CSR the spec adds, a CSR
# transported that the matrix marks excluded, or a carried-today CSR dropped from
# the ABI. See tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py for the exact checks and
# docs/csr_coverage.ipynb for the disposition of every CSR.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "python3 required"

out=$(python3 "$SCRIPT_DIR/check_coverage.py" 2>&1) || fail "coverage guard FAILED"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out"
ok "csr coverage guard: spec inventory == matrix == ABI (no drift)"

---
name: csr-transport-bringup
description: >
  Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given
  the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole
  pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence
  conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions,
  bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the
  reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify,
  and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a
  new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps
  gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported
  in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify
  field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up"
  explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test
  files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a
  new config of an existing core.
---

# CSR transport bring-up for a new Andes core

Inputs you need from the user (ask if missing):
- The AndeStar V5 SPA PDF for the core family (the repo carries
  `AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7.pdf` for the current cores).
- The engine name (e.g. `ax45mpv_premium`) and a built vsim checkout
  (`VSIM_BIN_DIR` in `config.env` points at its `build/`).
- Optionally the matching QEMU `-cpu` name for the oracle leg.

The goal: every CSR the core implements and the ROI can touch is restored at
resume, re-read at drain, and `--verify`-compared -- and every CSR the core
does NOT implement is gated off. Getting the gate wrong is SILENT at run
time: transport is one tolerant Abstract Command per CSR in both directions
(the Program Buffer carries only the V data sweep, the Tier-B vsetvl, and
L2C MMIO), so an over-claimed CSR just mirrors as zero. Caps truth is proven
by the reset-hart probe + the manifest completeness check, never by a run
"not crashing".

Work in this order. Each phase has a reference file with the details --
read it when you reach the phase, not before.

## Phase 0: establish ground truth (three sources)

Validation means connecting THREE sources per CSR -- the spec, the build
config, and the CPU core RTL -- and they speak different languages:
- CONFIG: `$VSIM_BIN_DIR/V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc` (the BUILD copy -- the
  `external/` source tree can differ) + `sim_<engine> --describe`.
- RTL: the CSR decoder's `existent_csr` equation (kv_core family:
  `andes_ip/kv_core/ucore/hdl/kv_csr_dec.v`). This is the Rosetta stone: it
  states each spec existence condition as a function of config params --
  the mapping neither document contains.
- SPEC: Phase 1 below.
Read `references/three-way-audit.md` -- the tutorial for connecting the
three and turning the result into the engine's test cases. Do not trust
QEMU: its gdbstub exposes CSRs the vsim RTL does not implement, and a caps
map built from QEMU over-claims them -- silently, since the tolerant
abstract transport mirrors an absent CSR as zero instead of faulting.

## Phase 1: mine the spec

Run `scripts/extract_csr_inventory.py <spec.pdf>` to refresh
`tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv` (needs PyMuPDF; use a venv). Then pull,
for each CSR the core claims: the IM Requirement (existence condition), the
Access Mode, and the reset value. The SPA has a fixed per-CSR layout and a
consolidated existence table (Table 13) -- see
`references/spec-mining.md` for the exact headers and extraction recipes.

## Phase 2: classify dispositions

Run `scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv` and
the guard `tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py`. The guard enforces
inventory == matrix == ABI (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`), so a CSR added to
the wire format without a disposition (or vice versa) fails loudly. New
transported CSRs are one X-macro line in `state_abi.h`
(`HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST` / `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST`); every consumer
(plugin drain, restore, drain re-read, verify) iterates the same list.

## Phase 3: bind capability gates

For each transported CSR, build the three-way translation row (spec
condition <-> RTL `existent_csr` term <-> config macros; see
`references/three-way-audit.md`), then encode it: a gate in the vsim repo's
`src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp` (address -> gate), the `_NDS_*` binding in
`andes_caps_config.hpp` (absent macro reads as "off" -- never a compile
error), and the same rule in the andesim mirror
`scripts/config_inc_to_andes_caps.py` (the parity guard keeps the two
honest). The gate must encode the RTL's existence term, not a
plausibly-related feature; three real bugs came from getting this wrong
(0x7D1, jvt, 0x7CF/PMNDS). Follow TDD: model the new engine's config shape
as a caps helper in `tests/hybrid/andes_caps.test.cpp` and write the
failing expectation first. Read `references/caps-gating.md` -- it carries
the gate-authoring rules and the write-prerequisite (setup ordering)
requirements.

## Phase 4: reset values and verify exclusions

Two reset-value sources exist and they legitimately differ:
- The SPA reset table (documentation; many fields are IM = implementation
  determined or DC = don't care).
- The EMPIRICAL baseline the simulator drains from the freshly reset hart
  (cached per engine build + ELF). The liveness gate compares against this
  one -- it is self-truthing, so spec IM/DC values need no manual table.

Where QEMU's reset differs from the engine's reset for a CSR the program
never writes (e.g. `msp_bound`, `milmb` enable bit), a strict compare
false-positives: add it to `andes_verify_excluded` in
`driver/state_diff.cpp` with a comment naming the divergence. Do NOT
exclude a CSR to hide a transport bug -- exclusion is only for
engine-implementation artifacts.

## Phase 5: validate (the ladder)

Run bottom-up; each rung catches what the one below cannot. The key
insight: the tolerant abstract path MASKS capability bugs (a faulting read
mirrors as zero, QEMU drains zero too, --verify falsely matches), so caps
truth needs its own empirical rung -- the reset-hart probe (`--probe`, a
checked read of every inventory CSR that reports an unimplemented one as
absent) cross-checked against the caps claim by the manifest completeness
check, which fails NAMING the CSR in either direction. Full commands,
expected outputs, and failure playbook: `references/validation.md`.

## Phase 6: register the engine (per-engine test completeness)

andesim is a commercial product: every supported engine BUILD must ship its
own complete, machine-checked CSR test artifacts -- and a rebuild of the
same core with a different config counts as a NEW registration (the
config.inc hash is the identity, so reuse is impossible by construction).
Four deliverables per engine build: the CSR manifest (every spec CSR:
implemented? transported? why? empirical reset value), a BOTH-direction
completeness check (over-claims AND under-claims -- claimed-but-absent per
the probe, or implemented-but-not-transported without a named exclusion --
must fail a script, not a human's memory), generated per-engine
write-survival fixtures, and a registration guard so an unregistered
engine fails loudly. Read
`references/engine-registration.md` for the contract, the file layout, and
the recipes (including what to build the first time the tooling is missing).

## Phase 7: commit and document

TDD and Tidy First apply: caps fixes, transport changes, and docs are
separate commits, each on a green suite. Update the vsim `ROADMAP.md`
known-limits and `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` (section 4.4 documents what --verify
compares). Update `tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv` through the classifier,
never by hand -- the guard checks policy == matrix.

# hybrid_sim

Workspace for the Andes hybrid simulator: QEMU 9.x (functional, MHz) + vsim
(SystemC + Verilator, cycle-accurate) sharing memory and architectural state
across a magic-CSR boundary.

Submodule:

- `include/` - the shared ABI (`andesim_abi` repo): the `hybrid_state_v1` wire
  contract under `include/hybrid/`, shared by the plugin, the driver, and vsim.

QEMU and vsim are integrated as prebuilt external binaries (set `QEMU_BIN_DIR` and
`VSIM_BIN_DIR` in `config.env`; see `config.env.example`), not vendored as
submodules. vsim sources live in the separate `hybrid_vsim` repo, built there.

## Quickstart

```sh
git clone --recursive https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim && cd hybrid_sim
bash scripts/build_all.sh
bash scripts/test_all.sh
```

Subcommands: `run`, `list`, `doctor`. Run `./andesim -h` for the
full list. See `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` Section 0.5 for a four-command
worked example, or Sections 1-5 for the developer-grade scripts
(`setup.sh`, `tests/e2e.sh`, `scripts/run_e2e.sh`).
`./andesim run --mode hybrid --print-memmap --engine <id>` prints the
hybrid-supported guest memory map (USER_GUIDE 2.6).

## Host dependencies

- C/C++ toolchain (clang preferred), CMake >= 3.20, ninja
- Python 3
- glib-2.0 dev (for the QEMU plugin)
- pkg-config
- a prebuilt `qemu-system-riscv64` (external; this repo no longer builds QEMU --
  set `QEMU_BIN_DIR` in `config.env`)
- a prebuilt vsim (external; this repo no longer builds vsim -- set `VSIM_BIN_DIR`
  in `config.env` to your vsim checkout's `build/` dir)

## Outputs

After `bash scripts/build_all.sh`:

- `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so` (+ `libhotloops.so`)

QEMU and vsim are external prebuilt binaries: `$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64`
and `$VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_*` (set both in `config.env`).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the user-facing andesim runtime (runtime/) for both arches. Produces:
#   build/runtime/       libandesim_runtime.a, crt0.o, andesim.ld, andesim.specs,
#                        include/andesim/ROI.h   (rv64; link -B build/runtime)
#   build/runtime/rv32/  the same, rv32          (rv32; link -B build/runtime/rv32)
# Users link with `-B <dir> -specs=andesim.specs` (USER_GUIDE.md section 5).
#
# rv64 always builds (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). rv32 builds too when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32
# is set. Self-contained: fills either toolchain from config.env (exported env
# wins), like setup.sh, so it runs without `source ./setup.sh` first.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
SRC="$ROOT/runtime"
CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"

[[ -f "$SRC/Makefile" ]] || { echo "missing $SRC/Makefile" >&2; exit 1; }

# Capture exported values (they win), then source config.env to fill any gaps.
ENV_TC64="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}"
ENV_TC32="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}"
if [[ -z "$ENV_TC64" || -z "$ENV_TC32" ]]; then
  if [[ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then
    [[ -f "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" ]] \
      || { echo "missing $CONFIG_TEMPLATE; cannot create $CONFIG_FILE" >&2; exit 1; }
    cp "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" "$CONFIG_FILE"
    echo "created $CONFIG_FILE from template -- edit it if your toolchains live elsewhere" >&2
  fi
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  . "$CONFIG_FILE"
fi
[[ -n "$ENV_TC64" ]] && HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$ENV_TC64"
[[ -n "$ENV_TC32" ]] && HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32="$ENV_TC32"

# rv64 (required).
if [[ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" || ! -d "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}/bin" ]]; then
  echo "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN unset or has no bin/; check $CONFIG_FILE" >&2
  exit 1
fi
make -C "$SRC" ARCH=rv64 TOOLCHAIN="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN"
echo "built: $ROOT/build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a (rv64)"

# rv32 (optional: needs the second toolchain).
if [[ -n "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}" && -d "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}/bin" ]]; then
  make -C "$SRC" ARCH=rv32 TOOLCHAIN="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32"
  echo "built: $ROOT/build/runtime/rv32/libandesim_runtime.a (rv32)"
else
  echo "skipped rv32 runtime: set HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 in $CONFIG_FILE to build it" >&2
fi
